title: 667. The Mystery of the Mona Lisa

sentences.en: This episode is brought to you by Lloyd's, which has been backing British ambition for over 250 years.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由劳埃德银行赞助播出，该行两百五十多年来一直支持着英国的雄心壮志。

sentences.en: Now, when you think about it, every dynasty in history has boiled down to two important elements, aspiration and action.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，历史上每一个王朝归根结底都离不开两个重要要素：渴望与行动。

sentences.en: And a classic example of this from British history, the rise of the House of Wessex,
sentences.zh: 英国历史上这方面的一个经典例子，就是威塞克斯王朝的崛起，

sentences.en: the family of Alfred the Great and his heirs, who, between them, established the United Kingdom of England.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德大帝及其继承人的家族，正是他们共同缔造了英格兰联合王国。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great story, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 没错，这是个很棒的故事，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Great lesson in leadership, I think, for anybody.
sentences.zh: 我想，这对任何人来说都是一堂极佳的领导力课。

sentences.en: So Alfred and his heirs, they marry idealism and pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿尔弗雷德和他的继承人们完美结合了理想主义与实用主义。

sentences.en: They're brilliant at alliances.
sentences.zh: 他们极其擅长结盟。

sentences.en: They're brilliant at managing power.
sentences.zh: 他们极其擅长掌控权力。

sentences.en: They're brilliant, of course, at managing their money, which is a key part of political leadership.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也极其擅长理财，而这是政治领导力的关键部分。

sentences.en: And of course, we are all reaping the rewards of their wisdom and foresight.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们现在都在享受他们智慧与远见带来的硕果。

sentences.en: When it's time to make your next move, you can bank on Lloyd's to be ready when you are.
sentences.zh: 当你准备好迈出下一步时，劳埃德银行随时准备为你保驾护航。

sentences.en: Because from new businesses to new homes and new life chapters, backed by generations of hope and ambition,
sentences.zh: 因为从新企业到新家园、人生新篇章，在数代人对希望与雄心的支持下，

sentences.en: you can see, Tom, why 14 million people trust Lloyd's to help make their dreams a reality.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，汤姆，为什么有一千四百万客户信任劳埃德银行，帮助他们将梦想化为现实。

sentences.en: Based on Lloyd's internal customer data from March 2026.
sentences.zh: 数据基于劳埃德银行2026年3月的内部客户数据。

sentences.en: Hers is the head upon which all the ends of the world are come, and the eyelids are a little weary.
sentences.zh: 她就像是集世间万物终点于一身的化身，眼睑略带倦意。

sentences.en: It is a beauty wrought out from within upon the flesh.
sentences.zh: 这是一种由内而外在肌肤上雕琢出的美。

sentences.en: The deposit, little cell by cell, of strange thoughts and fantastic reveries and exquisite passions.
sentences.zh: 那是通过奇异的想法、奇幻的遐想和精致的情感，细胞凝聚而成的沉淀。

sentences.en: Set it for a moment beside one of those white Greek goddesses or beautiful women of antiquity.
sentences.zh: 把她哪怕暂时放在那些古希腊的白色女神或古代的美丽女性身旁。

sentences.en: And how would they be troubled by this beauty into which the soul with all its maladies has passed?
sentences.zh: 带着各种隐疾的灵魂已然融入这种美中，又怎会不让她们为之动摇？

sentences.en: All the thoughts and experience of the world have etched and moulded there in that which they have of power to refine and make expressive the outward form,
sentences.zh: 世间所有的思想与经历都在那里蚀刻、塑造，展现出提炼并表现外在形态的力量，

sentences.en: the animalism of Greece, the lust of Rome, the mysticism of the Middle Age with its spiritual ambition and imaginative loves,
sentences.zh: 希腊的动物性、罗马的纵欲、中世纪带有精神雄心与浪漫爱恋的神秘主义，

sentences.en: the return of the pagan world, the sins of the Borgias.
sentences.zh: 异教世界的回归，波吉亚家族的罪孽。

sentences.en: She is older than the rocks among which she sits.
sentences.zh: 她比她所端坐的岩石还要古老。

sentences.en: Like the vampire, she has been dead many times and learned the secrets of the grave, and has been a diver in deep seas and keeps their fallen day about her,
sentences.zh: 如同吸血鬼一般，她经历过无数次死亡，知晓坟墓的秘密，曾潜入深海并让沉没的白昼环绕周身，

sentences.en: and trafficked for strange webs with eastern merchants, and as leader was the mother of Helen of Troy, and as Saint Anne the mother of Mary.
sentences.zh: 曾与东方商人交易奇异的织物，作为领袖她曾是特洛伊的海伦，作为圣安妮她曾是圣母玛利亚的母亲。

sentences.en: And all this has been to her, but as the sound of lyres and flutes, and lives only in the delicacy with which it has moulded the changing lineaments,
sentences.zh: 而这一切对她而言，不过是竖琴与长笛的声音，只存活于雕琢变幻线条的精致感之中，

sentences.en: and tinged the eyelids and hands.
sentences.zh: 为眼睑和双手染上色彩。

sentences.en: So that was the Victorian art critic, Walter Pater, in very Victorian prose.
sentences.zh: 这段极具维多利亚风格的散文，出自维多利亚时代的艺术评论家沃尔特·佩特之口。

sentences.en: And he was describing one of the most celebrated women who's ever existed.
sentences.zh: 而他所描述的是有史以来最著名的女性之一。

sentences.en: Her face familiar to probably not millions of people, but hundreds of millions, if not billions.
sentences.zh: 她的面孔大概不是被几百万人，而是被数亿甚至数十亿人所熟知。

sentences.en: A woman who's often regarded as the ultimate femme fatale.
sentences.zh: 一个常被视为终极蛇蝎美人的女性。

sentences.en: A woman into whom is poured, certainly according to Walter Pater, every woman who has ever existed.
sentences.zh: 一个按照沃尔特·佩特的说法，融入了有史以来所有女性的女性。

sentences.en: Beautiful, mysterious, exotic, erotic, and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 美丽、神秘、异国情调、色情而又危险。

sentences.en: Well, I say a woman, he's describing actually a painting of a woman.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我说的是一个女人，实际上他是在描述一幅画中的女性。

sentences.en: A painting which is surely the most well-known painting in the world.
sentences.zh: 一幅无疑是世界上最知名的画作。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: Tom, the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: You a fan?
sentences.zh: 你是它的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: Well, I've always taken it so for granted that I wouldn't really have called myself a fan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一直把它当成理所当然的存在，所以并不会真的称自己为粉丝。

sentences.en: Its fame is, and of itself, such a fascinating thing, that that's what prompted me to think that this might be a good topic for the rest of history.
sentences.zh: 它的名气本身就是一件如此迷人的事情，这正是我萌生将其作为“历史余音”后续话题的想法的原因。

sentences.en: But having plunged into the deep waters of the Mona Lisa's history, and explored the rocks that are older than time, among which she sits,
sentences.zh: 但当我深入探索《蒙娜丽莎》的历史深渊，探究她所端坐的那些比时间更古老的岩石时，

sentences.en: I am now definitely a fan, yes.
sentences.zh: 我现在绝对成了它的粉丝，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, tremendous.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: It's a painting that is a lot more interesting than I had thought.
sentences.zh: 这幅画比我想象的要有趣得多。

sentences.en: I mean, I think basically I've kind of been anesthetized to its beauty, and I guess that's true of lots of people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得自己基本上已经对它的美感到麻木了，我想很多人也是如此。

sentences.en: You kind of see it as a fridge magnet rather than as a painting, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你大概把它当成冰箱贴，而不是一幅画，对吧？

sentences.en: But it is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但它确实非常迷人。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons for its fame is actually that passage that you read.
sentences.zh: 它之所以闻名遐迩，原因之一其实就是你刚才读的那段文字。

sentences.en: It's one of the most kind of famous passages of purple prose in the whole of English literature.
sentences.zh: 那是整个英国文学中最著名的华丽辞藻段落之一。

sentences.en: He wrote that in 1869.
sentences.zh: 他是在1869年写下这段话的。

sentences.en: Back when he wrote that, the Mona Lisa was not remotely as famous as it is today.
sentences.zh: 在他写下这段话的时候，《蒙娜丽莎》远没有今天这么出名。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that the paintings that had cut through in the Victorian period were those that were very easily copied.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，在维多利亚时期能够产生影响的画作都是那些非常容易被复制的作品。

sentences.en: So paintings with kind of clear boundaries.
sentences.zh: 也就是边界清晰的画作。

sentences.en: But there's a quality to the Mona Lisa which seems to defy reproduction.
sentences.zh: 但《蒙娜丽莎》有一种似乎 defies 复制的特质。

sentences.en: It's actually very, very hard to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 实际上它非常非常难以复制。

sentences.en: And this wasn't for want of trying.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为人们没有尝试过。

sentences.en: People have been trying to capture the essence of this extraordinary painting right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，人们就一直在试图捕捉这幅非凡画作的精髓。

sentences.en: So there's a famous copy of it in the Prado, which was done while the Mona Lisa had only just been painted.
sentences.zh: 普拉多博物馆里就有一幅著名的临摹作品，是在《蒙娜丽莎》刚刚画完不久后创作的。

sentences.en: But it doesn't get its essence at all.
sentences.zh: 但它根本没有抓住这幅画的精髓。

sentences.en: Then going into the 18th, into the 19th century, they try and do it with copper plate prints.
sentences.zh: 到了18和19世纪，人们尝试用铜版画来复制。

sentences.en: Then, of course, photographs.
sentences.zh: 当然，后来又有了摄影技术。

sentences.en: But even photographers, apparently, to begin with, struggled to capture the Mona Lisa in their photographs because the technology just wasn't up to reproducing it.
sentences.zh: 但显然，起初连摄影师们都很难在照片中捕捉到《蒙娜丽莎》，因为当时的技术还不足以复制它。

sentences.en: And it's only by the 1880s that photography has evolved technologically enough to allow for kind of accurate photographs of the Mona Lisa to be reproduced on a mass scale.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪80年代，摄影技术才在技术上取得了足够的发展，允许人们大规模复制精确的《蒙娜丽莎》照片。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, of course, the image of the Mona Lisa gets spread across Europe, across the world.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，《蒙娜丽莎》的形象得以传遍欧洲、传遍世界。

sentences.en: And I think it is – I mean, you said maybe it's the most recognisable painting.
sentences.zh: 我认为它——我是说，你刚才说它可能是最具辨识度的画作。

sentences.en: I would say there's no doubt about it at all.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，这绝对毫无疑问。

sentences.en: It is the most recognisable painting that has ever been in the whole of history.
sentences.zh: 它是整个历史上有史以来最具辨识度的画作。

sentences.en: And yet, at first glance – well, I mean, as you say, at first glance, you barely notice it because it's ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 然而，乍一看——好吧，正如你所说，乍一看，你几乎注意不到它，因为它无处不在。

sentences.en: So you don't really think anything of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你根本不会去想它有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: It's part of the furniture.
sentences.zh: 它就像是家具的一部分。

sentences.en: But when you look at it, there's nothing remarkable about it.
sentences.zh: 但当你仔细端详它时，会发现它并没有什么非凡之处。

sentences.en: There's nothing exceptional about it compared with, for example, some of the paintings that you did on the Rest is History Club miniseries in Laura Cumming.
sentences.zh: 与你在劳拉·卡明参与的“历史余音”俱乐部迷你系列中讨论过的一些画作相比，它没有什么特别出众的地方。

sentences.en: A painting like Las Meninas by Velázquez is much more, you know, appears much more nuanced, much more layered, much more sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 像委拉斯开兹的《宫娥》这样的画作，你知道的，显得更有细微差别、更有层次感、更加成熟。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa is just a woman sitting on a balcony looking out at you.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》只是一个坐在阳台上望着你的女人。

sentences.en: What's so special, do you think, about this that makes it hard to reproduce?
sentences.zh: 你认为这幅画有什么特别之处，让它如此难以复制？

sentences.en: Before we get into that, we should just describe it for the three people perhaps in the world who've never seen it.
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨之前，我们应该为世界上那三位可能从未见过它的人描述一下。

sentences.en: So there's something distinctive about her pose.
sentences.zh: 她的姿势很有特点。

sentences.en: Distinctive, certainly, when it was painted.
sentences.zh: 在当时创作时，这绝对是与众不同的。

sentences.en: So she's kind of sitting in profile, but her torso has turned around so that her face is almost staring into the eyes of the person who is standing in front of the painting.
sentences.zh: 她侧身而坐，但躯干转了过来，使得她的脸几乎直视着站在画作前的人的眼睛。

sentences.en: Her face is pale.
sentences.zh: 她的脸色苍白。

sentences.en: She's got brown eyes.
sentences.zh: 她长着一双棕色的眼睛。

sentences.en: She's got quite full cheeks, kind of, she's certainly not thin.
sentences.zh: 她的脸颊相当饱满，怎么说呢，她绝对不瘦。

sentences.en: She has no eyebrows.
sentences.zh: 她没有眉毛。

sentences.en: She has long, delicately curling hair, but this is covered by an almost translucent veil.
sentences.zh: 她留着长而柔和微卷的头发，但被一层几乎半透明的面纱盖住。

sentences.en: She has a very plain, dark dress.
sentences.zh: 她穿着一件非常朴素的深色长裙。

sentences.en: She has no jewellery, no adornments of any kind.
sentences.zh: 她没有佩戴任何珠宝，也没有任何形式的装饰。

sentences.en: And, of course, the most famous thing about her expression, probably the most famous thing about the entire painting, is her smile.
sentences.zh: 当然，她表情中最著名的一点，可能也是整幅画中最著名的一点，就是她的微笑。

sentences.en: And we'll be coming to that.
sentences.zh: 我们待会儿会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, people go on about that.
sentences.zh: 对，人们总是对这一点津津乐道。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I don't even think it really is much of a smile.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，我甚至不觉得这算是什么明显的微笑。

sentences.en: If someone looked at me like that and said, I'm smiling at you, I'd be like, are you?
sentences.zh: 如果有人那样看着我说“我在对你笑”，我大概会想：你是在笑吗？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: That is part of the mystery, is that people respond to the smile in many different ways.
sentences.zh: 这就是神秘感的一部分，人们对这种微笑有各种各样的反应。

sentences.en: But just before we come to that, the one thing about the painting that is overtly fantastical is the landscape against which the Mona Lisa is set.
sentences.zh: 但在我们讨论这个之前，这幅画中唯一明显带有奇幻色彩的是《蒙娜丽莎》身后的风景。

sentences.en: So this is a landscape that's very barren, it's kind of wild, it's tortured.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当荒凉、野性且饱经沧桑的风景。

sentences.en: You have jagged mountains, rocks, lakes, and the only signs of a kind of human physical presence.
sentences.zh: 这里有参差不齐的山脉、岩石、湖泊，而人类活动存在的唯一迹象,

sentences.en: There's a winding road and there's an arched bridge crossing a river.
sentences.zh: 是一条蜿蜒的道路和一座横跨河流的拱桥。

sentences.en: Tom, I commend you for this because you made me look at the painting already in a new way.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我要表扬你，因为你让我以一种崭新的方式审视了这幅画。

sentences.en: I've never even noticed the background, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我以前从未注意到背景。

sentences.en: Okay, so if you're looking at it, the striking thing about the quality of the paint, and I think this is the reason why it is so difficult to reproduce, isn't the subject.
sentences.zh: 好了，如果你仔细观察它，颜料质感最引人注目的一点，也是我认为它如此难以复制的原因，并不是它的主体。

sentences.en: It's the way in which this woman and the landscape have been painted.
sentences.zh: 而是这个女人和风景的绘制方式。

sentences.en: Because there's a very distinctive quality to it, and it's traditionally described as fumato, as smoky.
sentences.zh: 因为这里有一种非常独特的特质，传统上被描述为晕涂法（sfumato），也就是烟雾状的晕染。

sentences.en: And the effect of this is brilliantly described by, certainly, the leading British expert on the Mona Lisa, who is Martin Kemp, who isn't the bassist from Spandau Ballet.
sentences.zh: 英国研究《蒙娜丽莎》的首席专家马丁·肯普——他不是斯潘道芭蕾乐队的贝斯手——对这种效果做了极其精彩的描述。

sentences.en: Not him.
sentences.zh: 不是那个人。

sentences.en: I think he's the professor of art at Oxford or something.
sentences.zh: 我想他是牛津大学的艺术教授什么的。

sentences.en: No, you're an Oxford doctorate.
sentences.zh: 不，你才是牛津博士。

sentences.en: Yeah, he actually is the same person.
sentences.zh: 对，其实他们是同一个人。

sentences.en: So Martin Kemp describes the effect of fumato as being the paradox of a precisely rendered indefiniteness.
sentences.zh: 因此，马丁·肯普将晕涂法的效果描述为“精确呈现的不确定性”这一悖论。

sentences.en: So it's not precise.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不是精确的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a sense of kind of smokiness to it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它有一种烟雾缭绕的感觉。

sentences.en: Now, how do you render indefiniteness precisely?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何精确地呈现这种不确定性呢？

sentences.en: This is the kind of question that already, by the beginning of the 19th century, was puzzling German idealist philosophers.
sentences.zh: 正是这种问题，早在19世纪初就让德国唯心主义哲学家们大伤脑筋。

sentences.en: So let's quote the most famous German idealist philosopher, who is Hegel.
sentences.zh: 让我们引用最著名的德国唯心主义哲学家黑格尔的话。

sentences.en: And he was lecturing in the 1820s on the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 他在19世纪20年代曾就文艺复兴发表过演讲。

sentences.en: Great to get Hegel on the show.
sentences.zh: 能在节目中请到黑格尔真棒。

sentences.en: Great to have Hegel back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴黑格尔再度做客。

sentences.en: So he wrote,
sentences.zh: 他写道：

sentences.en: Here is evident a supreme rounding.
sentences.zh: “这里明显呈现出一种极致的圆润。

sentences.en: Nowhere is there any harsh or sharp line.
sentences.zh: 任何地方都没有严厉或生硬的线条。

sentences.en: Transition is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 过渡无处不在。

sentences.en: Light and shadow are not effective as purely direct light and shadow, but they both shine into one another, just as an inner force works throughout an external thing.
sentences.zh: 光影并非纯粹作为直接的光影起作用，而是相互交融、彼此辉映，正如某种内在力量贯穿于外在事物之中。”

sentences.en: Now, what that means in practical terms for the impact of this portrait of Mona Lisa is that the corners of her eyes and of her mouth are blurred.
sentences.zh: 从实际效果来看，这意味着《蒙娜丽莎》肖像的眼角和嘴角是模糊的。

sentences.en: It's hard to get an exact sense of what they actually look like.
sentences.zh: 人们很难确切地看清它们到底长什么样。

sentences.en: And as we've mentioned, there are no visible eyebrows.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所提到的，画中没有可见的眉毛。

sentences.en: And this makes it difficult to read her expression.
sentences.zh: 这让人很难解读她的表情。

sentences.en: And you've already touched on the most famous puzzle.
sentences.zh: 你刚才已经提到了那个最著名的谜题。

sentences.en: Is there a smile at all?
sentences.zh: 这到底是不是一个微笑？

sentences.en: If it is a smile, is she looking happy?
sentences.zh: 如果这是一个微笑，她看起来是高兴吗？

sentences.en: Is she looking sad?
sentences.zh: 她看起来是悲伤吗？

sentences.en: Is it a knowing smile?
sentences.zh: 这是一个意味深长的微笑吗？

sentences.en: Is it a modest smile?
sentences.zh: 这是一个端庄的微笑吗？

sentences.en: Is this the smile of a Florentine matron?
sentences.zh: 这是一个佛罗伦萨贵妇的微笑吗？

sentences.en: Or is it the smile of a vampire who is older than the rocks among which she sits?
sentences.zh: 还是一个比她所端坐的岩石还要古老的吸血鬼的微笑？

sentences.en: See, to me, you know, I recognize that smile straight away.
sentences.zh: 你看，对我来说，你懂的，我一眼就能认出那种微笑。

sentences.en: It's the weak smile of somebody who's heard a joke about the Kaiser a thousand times.
sentences.zh: 那是某个听过一千遍关于德皇笑话的人脸上那种无力的微笑。

sentences.en: And is thinking, I should never have come to this Rest is History get together.
sentences.zh: 心里想着：我真不该来参加这个“历史余音”聚会。

sentences.en: This is awful.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Well, you see, there is the power of the sfumato, because each person will see in the smile what he or she.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是晕涂法的力量所在，因为每个人都会在这个微笑中看到他或她自己……

sentences.en: Yeah, what they fear.
sentences.zh: 是的，看到他们恐惧的东西。

sentences.en: Or perhaps desire.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是渴望的东西。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But certainly, this is where I think Walter Pater is coming in with his notion of her as, you know, a kind of timeless, infinite, vampiric figure.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，我认为沃尔特·佩特正是带着他那种将她视为永恒、无限、吸血鬼般人物的观念而来的。

sentences.en: The fact that there is a mystery to her, that her smile is something elusive and enigmatic and potentially tantalizing.
sentences.zh: 她身上存在着一种神秘感，她的微笑难以捉摸、充满enigmatic（谜一般）且潜在地勾人魂魄。

sentences.en: And it's this that really, since the 19th century, has made the Mona Lisa seem almost a sinister figure in the imaginings of many people.
sentences.zh: 正是这种特质，自19世纪以来，让《蒙娜丽莎》在许多人的想象中几乎变成了一个阴险的人物。

sentences.en: And the painting to be something that contains codes, clues, directions to something that seems to lurk just beyond human comprehension.
sentences.zh: 也让这幅画变成了一种包含密码、线索以及指向某种潜藏在人类理解力之外事物的指引的东西。

sentences.en: And this is an idea that, of course, is still going incredibly strong.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种观点至今仍然盛极一时。

sentences.en: And friend of the show, Dan Brown, he's notoriously all over it.
sentences.zh: 节目的老朋友丹·布朗，可以说是对此烂熟于心。

sentences.en: So in the Da Vinci Code, the Mona Lisa, he says, embodies the sacred feminine.
sentences.zh: 所以在《达·芬奇密码》中，他说《蒙娜丽莎》体现了神圣女性的力量。

sentences.en: And in the plot of the Da Vinci Code, the Mona Lisa is in the louvre behind its stained glass window.
sentences.zh: 而在《达·芬奇密码》的剧情中，《蒙娜丽莎》就挂在卢浮宫那扇彩色玻璃窗后面。

sentences.en: And a clue is found written in blood on this stained glass window.
sentences.zh: 而线索就用鲜血写在这扇彩绘玻璃窗上。

sentences.en: And even though the Mona Lisa actually doesn't feature very prominently in the plot of the Da Vinci Code, when they came to make a film and they wanted a poster,
sentences.zh: 尽管《蒙娜丽莎》在《达芬奇密码》的剧情中其实并没有占据多大分量，但当他们决定拍电影并需要一张海报时，

sentences.en: it's the Mona Lisa that is on the poster.
sentences.zh: 海报上用的正是《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And obviously, the reason for why the Mona Lisa is on the film poster is because it's the world's most famous painting.
sentences.zh: 很显然，《蒙娜丽莎》之所以会出现在电影海报上，是因为它是世界上最著名的画作。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons that it's the world's most famous painting is precisely because it seems so full of mystery,
sentences.zh: 它之所以能成为世界上最著名的画作之一，原因之一恰恰在于它似乎充满了神秘感，

sentences.en: a painting suited to a film about kind of codes and ancient mysteries.
sentences.zh: 这幅画非常适合一部涉及各种密码和古代神秘事物的电影。

sentences.en: So two obvious questions then.
sentences.zh: 那么，自然就会有两个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: So first of all, is it only famous because of the mystery rather than because of any other quality?
sentences.zh: 首先，它出名究竟是因为神秘感，还是因为它本身的某种品质？

sentences.en: And secondly, what actually behind all the stuff about the mystery and the murk and the smokiness, what actually do we know about it?
sentences.zh: 其次，抛开所有关于神秘、阴暗和朦胧的种种炒作不谈，我们对它到底了解多少？

sentences.en: So let's take the first one.
sentences.zh: 让我们先来看看第一个问题。

sentences.en: Is it so famous purely because of this sort of the questions rather than because of any innate quality?
sentences.zh: 它之所以如此出名，纯粹是因为这类疑问，而不是因为什么内在品质吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think that is the big question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这才是最大的问题。

sentences.en: And let's come to that later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再来探讨这个。

sentences.en: So we'll kind of explore what it is that has made the Mona Lisa as famous as it is.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨究竟是什么让《蒙娜丽莎》享誉如此之高。

sentences.en: And I think it's really interesting because it tells us a lot about the history of how conceptions of culture have evolved over the centuries,
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的很有趣，因为它向我们讲述了几个世纪以来文化观念如何演变的历程，

sentences.en: and particularly perhaps in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 或许在20世纪尤其如此。

sentences.en: Your second question, I mean, let's assume the Mona Lisa isn't a portrait of a vampire, then who is it a portrait of?
sentences.zh: 至于你的第二个问题，我是说，假设《蒙娜丽莎》画的不是吸血鬼，那她到底是谁的肖像？

sentences.en: When was the painting begun?
sentences.zh: 这幅画是什么时候开始创作的？

sentences.en: When was it finished?
sentences.zh: 又是什么时候完成的？

sentences.en: I mean, was it ever finished?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它真的完成过吗？

sentences.en: And these are all kind of pretty basic questions that have been furiously debated for centuries and centuries and centuries.
sentences.zh: 这些都是相当基础的问题，却被激烈地争论了整整好几个世纪。

sentences.en: But not unusual questions.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是什么罕见的问题。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Tom, not unusual questions.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: I mean, these are the questions that people ask about all kinds of Renaissance paintings, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是人们在面对各种文艺复兴时期的画作时会问的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: You know, who painted it?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，谁画的？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: When?
sentences.zh: 什么时候？

sentences.en: Where?
sentences.zh: 在哪里？

sentences.en: Who's the sitter?
sentences.zh: 模特是谁？

sentences.en: All of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think that the intensity of the controversy that seems to lie around these questions when it comes to the Mona Lisa is actually just another marker of how incredibly famous it is.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当涉及到《蒙娜丽莎》时，围绕这些问题所引发的争议之激烈，其实正是它究竟有多么闻名的又一个标志。

sentences.en: Because every art historian, everybody who aspires to be an art historian knows that if you come up with a new theory about the Mona Lisa,
sentences.zh: 因为每个艺术史学家、每一个立志成为艺术史学家的人都知道，如果你能提出关于《蒙娜丽莎》的新理论，

sentences.en: you'll immediately get it into the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 你马上就能登上各大报纸。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of incentive there to come up often with quite mad theories.
sentences.zh: 所以这就有一种动力，促使人们经常提出相当疯狂的理论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: However, there is one thing that we absolutely do know about the painting.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于这幅画，有一件事是我们绝对确定的。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is the identity of the person who painted it.
sentences.zh: 当然，那就是画家的身份。

sentences.en: And even Dan Brown gets that right because it's there in the title of his book.
sentences.zh: 甚至丹·布朗也没有搞错这一点，因为他的书名里就写着呢。

sentences.en: It's Leonardo.
sentences.zh: 这就是达芬奇。

sentences.en: Although he gets the name wrong.
sentences.zh: 尽管他把名字弄错了。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: He gets the name wrong because Leonardo da Vinci.
sentences.zh: 他把名字搞错了，因为列奥纳多·达·芬奇。

sentences.en: Da Vinci, I mean, I can't believe there are any listeners who don't know this.
sentences.zh: 达·芬奇，我的意思是，我简直不敢相信还有听众不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Da Vinci is not his surname.
sentences.zh: 达·芬奇并不是他的姓氏。

sentences.en: Da Vinci just means from Vinci, which is where he was born.
sentences.zh: 达·芬奇只是“来自芬奇”的意思，那是他出生的地方。

sentences.en: Like if Dan Brown wrote a book about you and he called it the From Salisbury Code.
sentences.zh: 就像如果丹·布朗写了一本关于你的书，然后把它叫做《来自索尔兹伯里密码》一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So Leonardo da Vinci, we know that he paints it.
sentences.zh: 所以列奥纳多·达·芬奇，我们知道这画是他画的。

sentences.en: And he, of course, is one of the great figures of European culture, an extraordinary man, I think, entirely deserving of his own series on the rest of history in due course.
sentences.zh: 当然，他是欧洲文化中伟大的人物之一，一个非凡的人，我认为他完全当得起在适的时候推出属于他自己的“历史的其余部分”系列节目。

sentences.en: But for now, let's zoom in on one particular moment in that extraordinary life of his.
sentences.zh: 但现在，让我们把镜头聚焦在他那非凡一生中的某一个特定时刻。

sentences.en: And it is April 1500.
sentences.zh: 那是1500年4月。

sentences.en: And we are in Florence, which is Leonardo's native city.
sentences.zh: 我们正身处佛罗伦萨，这是列奥纳多的大本营。

sentences.en: This is almost certainly where he'd been born 48 years before.
sentences.zh: 这几乎可以肯定就是他48年前出生的地方。

sentences.en: And he is the illegitimate son of a Florentine notary, Sir Piero da Vinci, who came from the small town of Vinci, which is about 20 miles west of Florence.
sentences.zh: 他是佛罗伦萨公证人皮耶罗·达·芬奇爵士的私生子，皮耶罗来自距离佛罗伦萨以西约20英里的小镇芬奇。

sentences.en: So hence the name.
sentences.zh: 所以名字由此而来。

sentences.en: And Leonardo, right from the beginning, everyone recognizes that he is an astonishing talent.
sentences.zh: 而列奥纳多，从一开始，所有人就 reconhe认识到他拥有惊人的才华。

sentences.en: So he gets apprenticed very early to a famous Florentine artist, works in his workshop.
sentences.zh: 因此他很早就拜入一位著名的佛罗伦萨艺术家门下当学徒，并在其作坊工作。

sentences.en: He qualifies as a master and he is recognized even in Florence, which is a city.
sentences.zh: 他获得了大师资格，甚至在佛罗伦萨这座城市里也得到了认可。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the archetype of a great center of culture, Renaissance Florence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，文艺复兴时期的佛罗伦萨是伟大文化中心的典范。

sentences.en: As a man of really stupefying talent and what strikes people as stupefying about him isn't necessarily his talent as an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他具有真正令人目瞪口呆的天赋，而最让人惊叹的倒不一定是他的艺术才华。

sentences.en: I think he is rated slightly below his younger contemporaries, Michelangelo and Raphael on that score, but the sheer range of his interests.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这方面，人们对他的评价略低于他较年轻的同代人米开朗琪罗和拉斐尔，而是他极其广泛的兴趣范围。

sentences.en: So he's a complete polymath.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个名副其实的全才。

sentences.en: He's not just a painter.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是个画家。

sentences.en: He's also a would-be engineer.
sentences.zh: 他还是一个志向远大的工程师。

sentences.en: He's a natural philosopher.
sentences.zh: 他是一位自然哲学家。

sentences.en: There is no limit to the things that he's interested in.
sentences.zh: 他感兴趣的事物可以说是无所不包。

sentences.en: And this, of course, makes him an object of great interest to the cultural elites in Florence at the time, which, Dominic, we've done a series on.
sentences.zh: 当然，这使他成为了当时佛罗伦萨文化精英们高度关注的对象，多米尼克，我们曾为此做过一个系列节目。

sentences.en: And this is the Medici and specifically Lorenzo the Magnificent, the guy who serves in the popular imagination as the archetype of the Florentine patrons of great art.
sentences.zh: 这就是美第奇家族，尤其是“豪华者”洛伦佐，在人们的想象中，他就是佛罗伦萨伟大艺术赞助人的原型。

sentences.en: Lorenzo took him up, didn't he, and used him, among other things, as a kind of ambassador, but also as a kind of gift.
sentences.zh: 洛伦佐重用了他，不是吗？不仅让他充当某种特使，还把他当作某种礼物派上用场。

sentences.en: So he sends him to Ludovico Schwarzer, who's the Duke of Milan.
sentences.zh: 于是他把他派给米兰公爵卢多维科·斯福尔扎。

sentences.en: Florence's relations with Milan, enormously important in this period.
sentences.zh: 佛罗伦萨与米兰的关系在这一时期极其重要。

sentences.en: And Schwarzer, who's a patron of the arts himself, is very taken with Leonardo, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而本身就是艺术赞助人的斯福尔扎对列奥纳多非常赏识，对吧？

sentences.en: And Leonardo basically ends up working for Schwarzer for about almost 20 years, 18 years.
sentences.zh: 所以列奥纳多基本上最后为斯福尔扎工作了将近20年，整整18年。

sentences.en: Yeah, 18 years in all.
sentences.zh: 对，总共18年。

sentences.en: So by 1500, Leonardo is returning from Milan via Venice to Florence.
sentences.zh: 因此到1500年时，列奥纳多正经由威尼斯从米兰返回佛罗伦萨。

sentences.en: He's done pretty well for himself in Milan.
sentences.zh: 他在米兰混得相当不错。

sentences.en: So he's famous as a great painter.
sentences.zh: 作为一名伟大的画家，他已经名声大噪。

sentences.en: He's done this mural, The Last Supper, very important in The Da Vinci Code, very important also in the history of Western art.
sentences.zh: 他画了壁画《最后的晚餐》，这在《达芬奇密码》中非常重要，在西方艺术史上也同样举足轻重。

sentences.en: And two very innovative portraits of women.
sentences.zh: 还有两幅极具创新性的女性肖像画。

sentences.en: And one of these portrays Ludovico Schwarzer's young mistress, Cecilia Gallerani.
sentences.zh: 其中一幅画的是卢多维科·斯福尔扎年轻的情妇切奇利娅·加莱拉尼。
zh_words: 卢多维科·斯福尔扎年轻

sentences.en: And she is shown rather coily, kind of fondling an ermine.
sentences.zh: 画中的她显得有些娇羞，正爱抚着一只白鼬。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Tabby's favourite picture, I think.
sentences.zh: 这也是塔比最喜欢的画，我想是的。

sentences.en: I think so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我也这么觉得，对。

sentences.en: She loves fondling an ermine.
sentences.zh: 她很喜欢爱抚白鼬。

sentences.en: But the other thing about Leonardo is that he's got a utilitarian value as well as an aesthetic one, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 但关于列奥纳多的另一点是，除了审美价值之外，他还有实用价值，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he's also designing all kinds of – I mean, obviously he's designing all his mad stuff like parachutes and helicopters, tanks.
sentences.zh: 因为他还在设计各种各样的——我的意思是，显然他设计了所有那些疯狂的东西，比如降落伞、直升机、坦克。

sentences.en: But he's designing kind of hydraulics projects and stuff and city works and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 但他也设计水利工程、城市建设以及诸如此类的项目。

sentences.en: And fortifications and defences and things like this.
sentences.zh: 还有防御工事、防御设施之类的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, your claim about him being a polymath is well borne out by all this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你关于他是全才的说法从这一切中得到了充分的证实。

sentences.en: I gather that the kind of the mad stuff, so the tanks and the helicopters, it's unlikely any of them would have worked even had the technology been available to make them work.
sentences.zh: 我听说那些疯狂的东西，比如坦克和直升机，即使当时有制造它们的技术，它们中的任何一个也几乎不可能运作。

sentences.en: But the fortifications and the canals and everything, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但防御工事、运河以及所有这些，绝对是切实可行的。

sentences.en: And that essentially is why Schwarzer loved him.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是斯福尔扎爱惨了他的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, the ability to paint his mistress fondling an ermine was a kind of an advantage.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，能画出他情妇爱抚白鼬的画像算是一种优势。

sentences.en: But it's the engineering that really makes Leonardo's fortune.
sentences.zh: 但真正让列奥纳多发家致富的其实是他的工程学才华。

sentences.en: And he returns to Florence pretty well off.
sentences.zh: 他带着相当丰厚的身家回到了佛罗伦萨。

sentences.en: So he's – four months before he arrives in Florence, he sends a very large sum of money, about 600 ducats, to a Florentine bank.
sentences.zh: 所以他——就在他抵达佛罗伦萨四个月前，他向一家佛罗伦萨银行汇了一大笔钱，大约600达克特。

sentences.en: So he'll have something there waiting for him when he returns to Florence.
sentences.zh: 这样当他回到佛罗伦萨时，就会有一笔钱在那里等着他。

sentences.en: And just to give people a sense of how much that is, 20 ducats will rent you a very nice house in the centre of Florence for a year.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家对这个金额有个概念，20达克特就足够在佛罗伦萨市中心租下一栋非常漂亮的房子住一年了。

sentences.en: So Leonardo, you know, he's done well for himself.
sentences.zh: 所以列奥纳多，你知道的，他过得很滋润。

sentences.en: But what did you say this was 1500?
sentences.zh: 但你刚才说这是哪一年？1500年吗？

sentences.en: So 1500, by the time he comes back, Florence's golden age has passed.
sentences.zh: 所以到1500年他回来的时候，佛罗伦萨的黄金时代已经过去了。

sentences.en: They've been through the whole business with the Bonfire of the Vanities and Savonarola.
sentences.zh: 他们经历了一整套关于“虚荣之火”和萨沃纳罗拉的动荡。

sentences.en: The Medici have actually been kicked out of Florence, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 美第奇家族实际上已经被赶出了佛罗伦萨，不是吗？

sentences.en: And Florence is a republic again.
sentences.zh: 而且佛罗伦萨又重新变成了一个共和国。

sentences.en: And the biggest development, you know, one of the great developments in medieval Italian or early modern Italian history,
sentences.zh: 而最大的发展，你知道的，中世纪意大利或早期现代意大利历史上的重大事件之一，

sentences.en: the French invasion of 1494 has thrown Italy into total tumult.
sentences.zh: 1494年的法国入侵让意大利陷入了彻底的混乱。

sentences.en: Schwarz has been kicked out in Milan.
sentences.zh: 斯福尔扎在米兰被赶下台了。

sentences.en: The French have been rampaging through the Italian peninsula and they are the big power brokers now.
sentences.zh: 法国人一直在意大利半岛上横冲直撞，他们现在成了大权在握的幕后推手。

sentences.en: And basically, Leonardo, that leaves Leonardo a bit adrift, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 基本上，这让列奥纳多陷入了一种随波逐流、无所适从的境地，不是吗？

sentences.en: He needs a new patron because he doesn't have the Medici, he doesn't have Schwarz.
sentences.zh: 他需要一个新的赞助人，因为他没有了美第奇家族，也没有了斯福尔扎。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's why he's left Milan, as you say, Schwarz has been kicked out.
sentences.zh: 对，所以这就是他离开米兰的原因，正如你所说，斯福尔扎被赶走了。

sentences.en: But the problem is that even though he's a very big name, I mean, he's famous across Italy, he does also bring a certain amount of baggage with him.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，尽管他名气很大，我是说他在整个意大利都很有名，但他同时也带来了一定程度的历史包袱。

sentences.en: So in particular, he has a reputation for never finishing projects.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他有一个从不完成项目的名声。

sentences.en: So Giorgio Vasari, who will write the first biography of Leonardo, famously says of Leonardo that he started many things and never finished them.
sentences.zh: 因此，将要撰写第一部列奥纳多传记的乔治·瓦萨里，对列奥纳多有一句名言，说他发起过很多事情却从未完成过。

sentences.en: And the most notorious example of this had happened in Milan, which was a massive equestrian monument to the father of Ludovico Sforza.
sentences.zh: 其中最臭名昭著的例子发生在米兰，那是为卢多维科·斯福尔扎的父亲建造的一座巨大的骑马纪念碑。

sentences.en: That ends up being aborted when the French invade Italy because the Milanese need the bronze that was going to be used for the mold.
sentences.zh: 当法国入侵意大利时，这个项目最终流产了，因为米兰人需要原本要用来做模具的青铜。

sentences.en: They need to turn it into artillery to try and stop the French.
sentences.zh: 他们需要把它铸造成大炮，以试图阻挡法国人。

sentences.en: It doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有成功。

sentences.en: And when the French occupy Milan, they shoot up the great clay model of this equestrian statue that Leonardo had made.
sentences.zh: 当法国人占领米兰时，他们开枪击碎了列奥纳多制作的这座巨大骑马雕像的粘土模型。

sentences.en: So there's nothing left of it.
sentences.zh: 所以什么都没留下。

sentences.en: And this casts a slight shadow over his reputation.
sentences.zh: 这给他的声誉蒙上了一层淡淡的阴影。

sentences.en: So there's a story that when Michelangelo, who is younger than Leonardo and should properly be showing him respect, when Michelangelo meets Leonardo,
sentences.zh: 因此有个故事说，当比列奥纳多年轻、本该对前辈表现出应有敬意的米兰格朗琪罗遇到列奥纳多时，

sentences.en: he scoffs at him and says that the casting of the bronze had been beyond Leonardo's technological abilities.
sentences.zh: 他对列奥纳多冷嘲热讽，说青铜铸造超出了列奥纳多的技术能力。

sentences.en: And I think that this is a kind of a reproach that he has to bear, however unfairly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是他不得不承受的一种指责，尽管很不公平。

sentences.en: There's also the problem that he hasn't actually done that many paintings while he was in Florence.
sentences.zh: 还有一个问题是，他在佛罗伦萨期间其实并没有创作多少画作。

sentences.en: And the most famous painting, The Last Supper, I mean, this isn't readily accessible for anyone from Florence,
sentences.zh: 而最著名的画作《最后的晚餐》，我的意思是，这并不是任何佛罗伦萨人都能轻易看到的，

sentences.en: and it's probably already starting to fade because Leonardo's experimented with mad kinds of paints.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能已经开始褪色了，因为列奥纳多一直在尝试各种疯狂的颜料。

sentences.en: So he's actively looking for commissions and not just to make money, but also, I think, as a way of advertising what he can do as an artist,
sentences.zh: 所以他一直在积极寻找委托，不仅是为了赚钱，而且我认为这也是一种宣传他作为艺术家的能力的方式，

sentences.en: because every painting will be able to serve him as a kind of calling card.
sentences.zh: 因为每一幅画都能成为他的一张名片。

sentences.en: And so the first two years that he's back in Florence, we know from his records that he is taking on a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 因此，从他的记录中我们得知，回到佛罗伦萨的前两年里，他接了大量的工作。

sentences.en: He's taking a lot of commissions.
sentences.zh: 他接了很多委托。

sentences.en: These commissions do not include the Mona Lisa because, as I say, we have detailed records.
sentences.zh: 这些委托并不包括《蒙娜丽莎》，因为正如我所说，我们有详细的记录。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa isn't mentioned in them.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》在其中并未被提及。

sentences.en: And in fact, it is a part of the mystery of the painting that the Mona Lisa isn't mentioned in any of Leonardo's surviving drawings, any of his surviving notebooks.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这也是这幅画神秘之处的一部分，《蒙娜丽莎》没有在列奥纳多任何现存的草图或笔记本中被提及。

sentences.en: So that, you know, that adds a certain quality of mystery to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这为它平添了几分神秘色彩。

sentences.en: So he goes on.
sentences.zh: 于是他继续前进。

sentences.en: He works, I mean, unbelievably.
sentences.zh: 他的工作量，我的意思是，简直难以置信。

sentences.en: One day we'll do a series on the Borgias.
sentences.zh: 总有一天我们会做一个关于博尔吉亚家族的系列节目。

sentences.en: And he works for Cesare Borgia, doesn't he, as chief engineer.
sentences.zh: 他曾为切萨雷·博尔吉亚工作过，不是吗，担任总工程师。

sentences.en: So making tanks and helicopters for the Borgias.
sentences.zh: 所以为博尔吉亚家族制作坦克和直升机。

sentences.en: So that's in 1502 through to the early months of 1503.
sentences.zh: 那是从1502年一直到1503年的头几个月。

sentences.en: And then 1503, the spring of 1503, he is back in Florence.
sentences.zh: 然后到了1503年，1503年春天，他又回到了佛罗伦萨。

sentences.en: Some critics and biographers think this is the point when he did the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 一些评论家和传记作家认为这就是他创作《蒙娜丽莎》的时间点。

sentences.en: Others like Kenneth Clark, who did the great Civilization BBC series at the end of the 60s.
sentences.zh: 另一些人，比如在60年代末制作了伟大的BBC《文明》系列的肯尼斯·克拉克。

sentences.en: He thought it might have been a year later, 1504.
sentences.zh: 他认为这可能是又过了一年，即1504年。

sentences.en: So let's say 1503, 1504, or possibly even a later date.
sentences.zh: 所以我们假设是1503年、1504年，甚至可能是更晚的时间。

sentences.en: That's when he does the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 那是他创作《蒙娜丽莎》的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, so this is a debate that, again, has been running and running and running.
sentences.zh: 对，所以这是一个再次争论不休、没完没了的话题。

sentences.en: So it's 1503 to perhaps 1511, 1512.
sentences.zh: 所以时间大概是从1503年到1511年、1512年左右。

sentences.en: This is the kind of the range of dates.
sentences.zh: 这就是大致的时间范围。

sentences.en: But the bigger question, which I suppose is allied to that, is who is the person in the picture?
sentences.zh: 但更大的问题，我想这也与之相关，那就是画中人究竟是谁？

sentences.en: And, I mean, the name Mona Lisa, it's later.
sentences.zh: 而且，我是说，“蒙娜丽莎”这个名字是后来才有的。

sentences.en: I mean, it becomes popularized in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它是在19世纪才流行起来的。

sentences.en: But it's first coined in, what, the 1540s by Giorgio Vasari, who you've already mentioned in his great book, The Lives of the Artists, the great biographer of Renaissance Italy.
sentences.zh: 但它最早是在1540年代由乔治奥·瓦萨里提出的——你刚才已经提到过他，他写了那本伟大的《艺术家列传》，是意大利文艺复兴时期伟大的传记作家。

sentences.en: Yeah, so kind of 160 portrait sketches of the artists of the age.
sentences.zh: 对，大概收录了那个时代160位艺术家的肖像草图。

sentences.en: Vasari's great hero is Michelangelo.
sentences.zh: 瓦萨里心目中的大英雄是米开朗基罗。

sentences.en: But he does give Leonardo a decent write-up.
sentences.zh: 但他也给了达芬奇不错的评价。

sentences.en: And so if we estimate that the amount of space that Vasari gives to an artist is a reflection of how much he esteems the artist, then Michelangelo's number one.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把瓦萨里给一位艺术家的篇幅看作是他对这位艺术家敬重程度的体现，那么米开朗基罗排在第一位。

sentences.en: Then Raphael.
sentences.zh: 然后是拉斐尔。

sentences.en: Then Giotto.
sentences.zh: 然后是乔托。

sentences.en: Much earlier painter, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一位更早的画家。

sentences.en: And then Leonardo.
sentences.zh: 然后是达芬奇。

sentences.en: So Leonardo is number four.
sentences.zh: 所以达芬奇排在第四位。

sentences.en: Pretty good podium.
sentences.zh: 领奖台阵容相当不错。

sentences.en: I mean, one of them is not getting a medal.
sentences.zh: 我是说，其中有一个人拿不到奖牌。

sentences.en: Leonardo not quite podiuming there, is he?
sentences.zh: 达芬奇没能真正站上领奖台，对吧？

sentences.en: He's just Miss Bronze.
sentences.zh: 他只拿了铜牌小姐。

sentences.en: So this is what Vasari has to say.
sentences.zh: 这就是瓦萨里的说法。

sentences.en: He mentions the Mona Lisa explicitly.
sentences.zh: 他明确提到了《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: He writes, Leonardo undertook to paint the portrait of the wife of Francesco del Giocondo, Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 他写道：“达芬奇承接了弗朗切斯科·德尔·焦孔多的妻子蒙娜·丽莎的肖像画。”

sentences.en: So, I mean, there's one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就有一个问题。

sentences.en: It's not the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 它不叫“蒙娜丽莎”（The Mona Lisa）。

sentences.en: It's the Mona Lisa properly.
sentences.zh: 应该准确地叫“莫娜·丽莎”（Mona Lisa）。

sentences.en: But it gives us the name.
sentences.zh: 但这给我们提供了名字。

sentences.en: And Mona Lisa is Madonna Lisa.
sentences.zh: “Mona Lisa”就是“Madonna Lisa”。

sentences.en: So my lady Lisa.
sentences.zh: 也就是“我的丽莎女士”。

sentences.en: But that sentence also gives us the name that is used in Italy and in France.
sentences.zh: 但这句话也给我们提供了在意大利和法国使用的名字。

sentences.en: So in Italy, it's La Gioconda.
sentences.zh: 所以在意大利，它叫“La Gioconda”。

sentences.en: In France, it's La Gioconde.
sentences.zh: 在法国，它叫“La Gioconde”。

sentences.en: And there's a pun there.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个双关语。

sentences.en: So it's the feminine form of Lisa's husband's name.
sentences.zh: 它是丽莎丈夫姓氏的女性形式。

sentences.en: So essentially, it's kind of Mrs. Giocondo, La Gioconda.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，它有点像焦孔多太太，也就是La Gioconda。

sentences.en: But Gioconda and Gioconde, they mean in Italian and French respectively, kind of happy, cheerful, joyous.
sentences.zh: 但Gioconda和Gioconde在意大利语和法语中分别意味着快乐、高兴、喜悦。

sentences.en: And Vasari implies in his life of Leonardo that Leonardo leaned into this pun and that Mona Lisa's smile was key to his vision of the painting right from the very start.
sentences.zh: 瓦萨里在他的达芬奇传记中暗示，达芬奇利用了这个双关语，而且蒙娜丽莎的微笑从一开始就是他构思这幅画的核心。

sentences.en: So Vasari writes, while he was painting Mona Lisa, who was a very beautiful woman, he had her constantly entertained by singers,
sentences.zh: 所以瓦萨里写道：当他在画一位绝色佳人蒙娜丽莎时，他让歌手、

sentences.en: musicians and jesters so that she would be merry and not look melancholic as portraits often do.
sentences.zh: 音乐家和小丑不断地逗她开心，好让她保持欢乐，而不会像肖像画那样通常显得忧郁。

sentences.en: As a result, in this painting of Leonardo's, there was a smile so enchanting that it was more divine than human.
sentences.zh: 因此，在达芬奇的这幅画中，出现了一种如此迷人的微笑，以至于它与其说是人间凡品，不如说是神仙之姿。

sentences.en: And those who saw it marveled to find it so similar to that of the living original.
sentences.zh: 那些看到它的人都惊叹它与活生生的本尊如此相似。

sentences.en: I mean, I think, again, that's attributing the smile with more jollity than the painting deserves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这同样是给这个微笑赋予了比画作本身更多的欢乐。

sentences.en: Anyway, that anecdote may not even be true, right?
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这则轶事甚至可能不是真的，对吧？

sentences.en: Possibly, but possibly not, because when Vasari wrote up that anecdote,
sentences.zh: 有可能，但也可能不是，因为当瓦萨里写下这则轶事时，

sentences.en: he was living in Florence just a short distance from the Giocondo family home at a time when Mona Lisa was still alive.
sentences.zh: 他就住在佛罗伦萨，距离焦孔多一家的住宅不远，当时蒙娜丽莎还活着。

sentences.en: So it is perfectly possible that he got that directly from La Gioconda's mouth.
sentences.zh: 所以完全有可能他是直接从La Gioconda本人那里听到这个说法的。

sentences.en: I mean, we can't know, but it's possible, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们无法确知，但我想这是可能的。

sentences.en: So who is she?
sentences.zh: 那么她是谁？

sentences.en: Who's her husband?
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫是谁？

sentences.en: What's going on there?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I mean, he's literally called Mr. Happy, but isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的名字字面意思就叫“快乐先生”，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, as well he should be, because Francesco del Giocondo is doing very well for himself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他也确实配得上这个名字，因为弗朗切斯科·德尔·焦孔多事业非常成功。

sentences.en: So he's very ambitious.
sentences.zh: 所以他很有野心。

sentences.en: He's very upwardly mobile and he's becoming incredibly rich.
sentences.zh: 他很有上升空间，而且变得极其富有。

sentences.en: Of humble background, his grandfather had begun as an artisan in the barrel making business, and he ends up running an entire barrel making empire.
sentences.zh: 他出身卑微，他的祖父最初是做木桶生意的工匠，最后却经营起了一个庞大的木桶制造帝国。

sentences.en: Then Francesco's father had moved on from the barrel making into textiles, which is the obvious place that you go for kind of high-end products, much more money to be made.
sentences.zh: 随后，弗朗切斯科的父亲从木桶制造转向了纺织品，这是追求高端产品顺理成章的行业，能赚到更多的钱。

sentences.en: And Giocondo himself then expands into silks, into money lending, and into sugar.
sentences.zh: 焦孔多本人随后将业务扩展到丝绸、放贷和糖业。

sentences.en: So this is the early days of the Atlantic sugar economy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是大西洋糖业经济的早期阶段。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And it has been thought that perhaps Mona Lisa had access to lots of sugar and her teeth rotted, and this is why she's not showing her teeth.
sentences.zh: 人们曾认为，也许蒙娜丽莎有机会接触到大量的糖，导致牙齿腐烂，这就是她为什么不露齿而笑的原因。

sentences.en: And that's one of the clues to the mystery of the smile.
sentences.zh: 这也是破解微笑之谜的线索之一。

sentences.en: That's really trying too hard.
sentences.zh: 这实在有点过于牵强了。

sentences.en: But this is a very familiar Florentine journey.
sentences.zh: 但这是佛罗伦萨人非常熟悉的奋斗历程。

sentences.en: You start like the Medici did.
sentences.zh: 你的起步就像美第奇家族一样。

sentences.en: You make money in one thing, then you move into – I mean, textiles, wool is what Florentine money is based on.
sentences.zh: 你先在某个领域赚钱，然后涉足——我的意思是，纺织品，羊毛是佛罗伦萨财富的基础。

sentences.en: And then you move into banking or money lending or whatever, and you diversify.
sentences.zh: 然后你涉足银行业、放贷或其他领域，进行多元化经营。

sentences.en: So what Francesco was doing is absolutely standard.
sentences.zh: 所以弗朗切斯科所做的事情完全是标准操作。

sentences.en: And then he does the standard thing, which is that he invests a lot of his money into land, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 然后他做了标准的事情，那就是把大量的钱投资在土地上，对吧？

sentences.en: So especially now that the war is broken out with the French, and Italy is absolutely being ravaged and ripped apart,
sentences.zh: 特别是现在与法国的战争已经爆发，意大利正在被彻底蹂躏和撕裂，

sentences.en: it makes sense to invest in property and in land because that is the safest possible bet.
sentences.zh: 投资房产和土地是合乎情理的，因为那是最大稳妥的选择。

sentences.en: And, of course, what you also do – and this is a timeless story, I mean, we see it so much in English history as well – is that if you are socially mobile from a humble background,
sentences.zh: 当然，你还会做的一件事——这是一个永恒的故事，我的意思是我们在英国历史中也经常看到——那就是如果你出身卑微却实现了社会阶层上升，

sentences.en: you invest in an upper-class wife.
sentences.zh: 你就会投资娶一个上流社会的妻子。

sentences.en: And this is what Francesco does by marrying Lisa Gerardini,
sentences.zh: 这就是弗朗切斯科迎娶丽莎·格拉迪尼的原因，

sentences.en: because Lisa Gerardini is from an ancient Tuscan family that ranked as one of the original founders of the Florentine Republic.
sentences.zh: 因为丽莎·格拉迪尼来自一个古老的托斯卡纳家族，该家族被列为佛罗伦萨共和国的最初奠基人之一。

sentences.en: So a tremendous aristocratic pedigree.
sentences.zh: 所以有着极其显赫的贵族血统。

sentences.en: It is obviously a bit embarrassing for Lisa that she has to marry the grandson of a barrel maker.
sentences.zh: 对于丽莎来说，嫁给一个木桶匠的孙子显然有点尴尬。

sentences.en: But her father is not a good businessman.
sentences.zh: 但她的父亲并不是一个优秀的商人。

sentences.en: He's running short of money.
sentences.zh: 他资金短缺。

sentences.en: He needs money.
sentences.zh: 他需要钱。

sentences.en: And so he essentially sells Lisa to Francesco.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是把丽莎“卖”给了弗朗切斯科。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's a good marriage.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一桩不错的婚姻。

sentences.en: So Lisa is 15 when she marries Francesco.
sentences.zh: 丽莎嫁给弗朗切斯科时只有15岁。

sentences.en: Francesco is 30, and she is his second wife, and as we've heard, will end up outliving him.
sentences.zh: 弗朗切斯科30岁，她是他的第二任妻子，正如我们所听说的，她最终比他活得还久。

sentences.en: And I think that although the context for the marriage is a mercenary one, it seems to have been a relatively successful marriage.
sentences.zh: 我认为，尽管这桩婚姻的背景带有功利色彩，但它似乎是一桩相对成功的婚姻。

sentences.en: So Francesco keeps his side of the bargain by becoming fabulously rich, and Lisa sticks to hers by having lots of children.
sentences.zh: 所以弗朗切斯科通过变得极其富有兑现了他的承诺，而丽莎则通过生了许多孩子兑现了她的承诺。

sentences.en: And she has six in all.
sentences.zh: 她一共生了六个孩子。

sentences.en: Four of them survive infancy.
sentences.zh: 其中四个活到了成年。

sentences.en: And she also, she brings up a son of Francesco's by his first wife.
sentences.zh: 她还抚养了弗朗切斯科与前妻所生的一个儿子。

sentences.en: And again, their relationship seems to have been very good.
sentences.zh: 同样，他们的关系似乎也非常好。

sentences.en: All the evidence points to the fact that she was a very kind and supportive stepmother.
sentences.zh: 所有的证据都表明，她是一位非常善良和支持继子的继母。

sentences.en: There is one scandal which erupts in 1512, and it's focused on Lisa's daughter Camilla, who the year before, so in 1511, had become a nun at the age of 12.
sentences.zh: 1512年爆发了一桩丑闻，焦点是丽莎的女儿卡米拉。前一年，也就是1511年，卡米拉在12岁时成为了一名修女。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's quite early.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这年龄确实很小。

sentences.en: But it's a way, essentially, of avoiding having to pay a dowry for her.
sentences.zh: 但这基本上是避免为她支付嫁妆的一种方式。

sentences.en: So you either marry her off or you park her in a nunnery.
sentences.zh: 所以你要么把她嫁出去，要么把她送进修道院。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's what they do with Camilla.
sentences.zh: 他们就是这样对待卡米拉的。

sentences.en: And in 1512, four men, including Madley, a brother of the Cardinal of Pavia, are reported to have climbed up a ladder into the convent where Camilla was installed.
sentences.zh: 在1512年，据报道有四个男人（其中包括帕维亚红衣主教的兄弟马德利）顺着梯子爬进了卡米拉所在的修道院。

sentences.en: And two nuns, it is said, were waiting for them.
sentences.zh: 据说当时有两名修女在等候他们。

sentences.en: And the intruders, I quote, touched the breasts of the said nuns.
sentences.zh: 这些闯入者，我引用原话：“抚摸了上述修女的胸部。”

sentences.en: And there was apparently lots of fondling and groping.
sentences.zh: 显然有大量的抚摸和猥亵行为。

sentences.en: And Camilla is said to have been one of these two nuns.
sentences.zh: 据说卡米拉就是这两名修女之一。

sentences.en: And the four men were found guilty, but the two nuns were absolved.
sentences.zh: 这四个男人被判有罪，但两名修女被宣告无罪。

sentences.en: So a whiff of scandal, but perhaps no more than that.
sentences.zh: 所以有一丝丑闻的气息，但也仅此而已。

sentences.en: But apart from that, Lisa's life is pretty uneventful, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 除此之外，丽莎的一生相当平静，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, as you said, Francesco, 15 years her senior, he dies in 1537.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，比她大15岁的弗朗切斯科于1537年去世。

sentences.en: And in his will, he says she is his beloved, noble spirit, a faithful wife.
sentences.zh: 他在遗嘱中称她为他心爱的、高贵的灵魂、一位忠实的妻子。

sentences.en: She lives to a pretty good age for the time, 70.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，她活到了相当高寿的年龄——70岁。

sentences.en: She says she dies about 12 or 13 years later.
sentences.zh: 据说她在大约12或13年后去世。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly when.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道具体时间。

sentences.en: And that's all we know.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所知道的一切。

sentences.en: That's all we know of this character.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对这个人物的全部了解。

sentences.en: Which is amazing, because if she is the person in the Mona Lisa, then her face has a claim to be the most famous face of anyone who's lived in the whole of history,
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了，因为如果她就是《蒙娜丽莎》中的那个人，那么她的脸完全可以号称是整个人类历史上最著名的一张脸，

sentences.en: which is a kind of jaw-dropping thought.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让人惊掉下巴的想法。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But is she the woman?
sentences.zh: 但她真的是那个女人吗？

sentences.en: Because there are some critics who say this is not the woman.
sentences.zh: 因为有一些评论家说这不是那个女人。

sentences.en: She may not have existed at all.
sentences.zh: 她可能根本不存在。

sentences.en: This may be a fictional person.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个虚构的人物。

sentences.en: This may be a kind of just a generic embodiment of female beauty or of feminine elegance and grace or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这可能只是女性美、女性优雅风度或某种特质的泛泛化身。

sentences.en: Because, for example, there is no record of Leonardo having been paid by anybody for this painting, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，举个例子，没有任何记录表明达芬奇曾因这幅画收到过任何人的报酬，对吧？

sentences.en: And if he had done it for a rich patron, you would assume he would have been paid and he would have kept the receipt.
sentences.zh: 如果他是为一个富有的赞助人画的，你会认为他应该拿到报酬并且会保留收据。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he seems to have kept the painting with him until he died.
sentences.zh: 对，而且他似乎一直把这幅画带在身边，直到去世。

sentences.en: We've got that landscape, which is not a realistic landscape.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了那个风景，那不是一个真实的风景。

sentences.en: It's not a landscape that anyone can identify.
sentences.zh: 那不是任何人能认出的风景。

sentences.en: So, is this fantastical background painted in that way because it's appropriate to a woman who also is invented?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个奇幻的背景之所以这样画，是因为它适合一个同样是被虚构出来的女性吗？

sentences.en: And we do know from his notebooks that Leonardo was very interested in the kind of the notion of there being ideal beauty.
sentences.zh: 我们从他的笔记中确实知道，达芬奇对“理想美”的概念非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: Is the Mona Lisa not a real person at all?
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》根本就不是真人吗？

sentences.en: But what if she's a real person?
sentences.zh: 但如果她是一个真人呢？

sentences.en: I think that certainly for the past 200 years, there's been a feeling that the Mona Lisa is a bit boring.
sentences.zh: 我认为，至少在过去的200年里，人们一直有一种感觉，觉得《蒙娜丽莎》有点无聊。

sentences.en: I mean, she's just the wife of an Italian businessman.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她只是一个意大利商人的妻子。

sentences.en: Couldn't she be someone slightly more interesting?
sentences.zh: 难道她不能是一个稍微有趣一点的人吗？

sentences.en: So, there have been various candidates.
sentences.zh: 所以，曾有过各种候选人。

sentences.en: So, one of them is a woman called Pacifica Brandano.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是一个名叫帕西菲卡·布兰达诺的女人。

sentences.en: And she was the mistress of the son of Lorenzo the Magnificent, a guy called Giuliano de' Medici.
sentences.zh: 她是“豪华者洛伦佐”的儿子的情妇，那个人叫朱利亚诺·德·美第奇。

sentences.en: And he ends up returning to Florence, re-establishing Medici rule.
sentences.zh: 他最终返回佛罗伦萨，重建了美第奇家族的统治。

sentences.en: And he's essentially the kind of the autocrat of Florence between 1513 and 1516.
sentences.zh: 在1513年至1516年期间，他基本上是佛罗伦萨的独裁者。

sentences.en: Why does anyone think that the Mona Lisa might be this woman, Pacifica Brandano?
sentences.zh: 为什么有人会认为《蒙娜丽莎》可能是这个名叫帕西菲卡·布兰达诺的女人？

sentences.en: There's actually quite a good reason.
sentences.zh: 其实有一个很好的理由。

sentences.en: It's because the only person that we know of who saw the Mona Lisa in the lifetime of Leonardo and described it in writing,
sentences.zh: 因为据我们所知，在达芬奇生前唯一见过《蒙娜丽莎》并在文字中对其进行描述的人，

sentences.en: he claimed that the painting had been commissioned by Giuliano.
sentences.zh: 他声称这幅画是朱利亚诺委托创作的。

sentences.en: And if so, then wouldn't it be his mistress?
sentences.zh: 果真如此的话，那难道不应该是他的情妇吗？

sentences.en: Then there's another much more famous woman who is identified with the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个更著名的女人被认为与《蒙娜丽莎》有关。

sentences.en: And this is Isabella d'Este, who was the Marquise of Mantua.
sentences.zh: 这就是曼图亚侯爵夫人伊莎贝拉·德·埃斯特。

sentences.en: And she's the most famous, the most celebrated female patron of the arts in the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 她是文艺复兴时期最著名、最受赞誉的女性艺术赞助人。

sentences.en: And again, there are reasons for thinking that it might be her.
sentences.zh: 同样，有理由认为她可能就是画中人。

sentences.en: So, she was always imploring Leonardo to paint her portrait.
sentences.zh: 因为她曾屡次恳求达芬奇为她画肖像。

sentences.en: Leonardo actually went to Mantua and made sketches of her.
sentences.zh: 达芬奇确实去过曼图亚并为她画过素描。

sentences.en: We've said that the backdrop to the Mona Lisa, the landscape, is fantastical.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，《蒙娜丽莎》的背景——也就是那片风景，是非常奇幻的。

sentences.en: Assuming that it isn't, assuming that it is actually a portrait of somewhere in Italy, it might be the Dolomites.
sentences.zh: 假设它不是奇幻的，假设它实际上是意大利某个地方的肖像，那可能会是多洛米蒂山。

sentences.en: I mean, it's much more likely to be the Dolomites than Tuscany.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比起托斯卡纳，它更有可能是多洛米蒂山。

sentences.en: And Mantua is quite near the Dolomites.
sentences.zh: 而且曼图亚离多洛米蒂山很近。

sentences.en: And also, in the painting, she's seated on a chair with an armreSt.
sentences.zh: 另外，在画中，她坐在一把带扶手的椅子上。

sentences.en: And the armrest apparently is often used to symbolise a ruler.
sentences.zh: 而这个扶手显然经常用来象征统治者。

sentences.en: I think the way that you're narrating that suggests to me that you absolutely do not believe it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你讲述的方式让我觉得你绝对不相信这种说法。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't look like the Dolomites at all.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这看起来一点也不像多洛米蒂山。

sentences.en: I think that there is a slight quality of people not wanting to believe that Shakespeare wrote Shakespeare's plays.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一种微妙的心理，人们就是不愿意相信莎士比亚写了莎士比亚的戏剧。

sentences.en: And it would be much more fun if it was the Earl of Oxford or Christopher Marlowe or someone.
sentences.zh: 如果作者是牛津伯爵、克里斯托弗·马洛或其他什么人，那就会有趣得多。

sentences.en: That is exactly what I thought when you started to down this line.
sentences.zh: 当你顺着这个思路说下去时，我脑子里想的就是这个。

sentences.en: I thought, this is exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 我想，这完全就是那么回事。

sentences.en: People just do not want a humdrum explanation.
sentences.zh: 人们就是不想要一个平淡无奇的解释。

sentences.en: And they're groping desperately for something exotic.
sentences.zh: 他们拼命地想要寻找一些异国情调的东西。

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's continue with some slightly more exotic ones.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们继续讨论一些更有异国情调的观点。

sentences.en: So, Sigmund Freud, guess who he thinks the Mona Lisa is.
sentences.zh: 那么，西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，你猜他认为《蒙娜丽莎》是谁。

sentences.en: Amaze me and tell me that it's not his mother.
sentences.zh: 惊艳我一下，告诉我那不是他母亲。

sentences.en: It is his mother.
sentences.zh: 这就是他母亲。

sentences.en: So, Freud suggested that the smile, this famous smile, was inspired by Leonardo's childhood memories of his mother's smile.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗洛伊德认为，这种微笑，这个著名的微笑，灵感来自于列奥纳多对母亲微笑的童年记忆。

sentences.en: Sometimes a smile is just a smile, Sigmund.
sentences.zh: 有时候，微笑就只是微笑，西格蒙德。

sentences.en: Yeah, sometimes.
sentences.zh: 是的，有时候是的。

sentences.en: Another very popular theory recently is that it's this guy, Salai, who was Leonardo's apprentice, his friend, worked in his workshop, and was almost certainly his lover.
sentences.zh: 最近另一个非常流行的理论是，画中人是这家伙——萨莱，他是列奥纳多的学徒、朋友，在他的作坊里工作，几乎可以肯定是他的情人。

sentences.en: Hold on, Salai's a bloke?
sentences.zh: 等等，萨莱是个男的？

sentences.en: Salai's a bloke.
sentences.zh: 萨莱是个男的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, this is a stretch.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这有点勉强。

sentences.en: So, Salai is, you know, he serves Leonardo as a model for his painting of John the Baptist, which is in the Louvre, together with the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，萨莱曾担任列奥纳多绘制《施洗者约翰》的模特，这幅画和《蒙娜丽莎》一起收藏在卢浮宫里。

sentences.en: He provides the model for a sketch of an angel.
sentences.zh: 他为一幅天使的草图提供了模特原型。

sentences.en: And the idea that the Mona Lisa might be another portrait of Salai was proposed 15 years ago by an Italian art historian called Silvano Vincetti.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》可能是萨莱的另一张肖像画这一观点，是15年前由一位名叫西尔瓦诺·温切蒂的意大利艺术史学家提出的。

sentences.en: The reason that he advances this is that Vincetti says that the Mona Lisa's facial features do resemble those of Salai,
sentences.zh: 他提出这一论点的理由是，温切蒂称《蒙娜丽莎》的面部特征确实与萨莱的很相似，

sentences.en: and you can see them if you compare it to Leonardo's painting of John the BaptiSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它与列奥纳多的《施洗者约翰》进行对比，你就能看出来。

sentences.en: Also, he says that you can see the letter S in Mona Lisa's eyes if you look very closely and squint and stand on your head while you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 此外，他还说，如果你仔细观察、眯起眼睛，同时倒立着看，你就能在蒙娜丽莎的眼睛里看到字母S。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, good luck doing that in the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 是啊，祝你在卢浮宫里这么做时好运吧。

sentences.en: And we compared it to Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 我们把它和莎士比亚进行了对比。

sentences.en: There was a guy, wasn't there, who wanted to dig up Shakespeare's body to prove that it wasn't actually Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 曾经有个家伙，不是吗？他想挖出莎士比亚的尸体，来证明那其实不是莎士比亚。

sentences.en: And Vincetti, he's very much on that groove because he wanted to go to the site where Lisa Gherardini had been buried and to dig her up and to find her skull,
sentences.zh: 而温切蒂完全就是这个路数，因为他想去丽莎·盖拉迪尼安葬的地方去把她挖出来，找到她的头骨，

sentences.en: use it to reconstruct her features, and thereby prove that she couldn't have been the sitter in the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 用它来重构她的面部特征，从而证明她不可能是《蒙娜丽莎》里的模特。

sentences.en: Then two final theories, just before we come to the break.
sentences.zh: 然后是最后两个理论，就在我们进入中场休息之前。

sentences.en: One theory is the Mona Lisa is a portrait of Leonardo himself.
sentences.zh: 其中一个理论是，《蒙娜丽莎》是列奥纳多本人的自画像。

sentences.en: And this was first suggested back in 1913 by a French painter called Maurice Weil.
sentences.zh: 这最早是在1913年由一位名叫莫里斯·韦尔的法国画家提出的。

sentences.en: And he argued that the lower half of the face is female, but the upper half is Leonardo's.
sentences.zh: 他认为脸的下半部分是女性的，但上半部分是列奥纳多的。

sentences.en: And in 1987, an American artist called Lillian Schwartz made a famous computer mashup of the Mona Lisa with the self-portrait of Leonardo, the kind of famous one.
sentences.zh: 而在1987年，一位名叫莉莲·施瓦茨的美国艺术家将《蒙娜丽莎》与列奥纳多的自画像（也就是那种著名的自画像）进行了著名的电脑合成。

sentences.en: It's presumed to be self-portrait.
sentences.zh: 人们推测那是自画像。

sentences.en: We don't know for sure, but it's the one where he kind of looks like Gandalf.
sentences.zh: 我们无法百分之百确定，但那就是他看起来有点像甘道夫的那张画。

sentences.en: He's got the long white hair and, you know, they match up pretty well and can kind of see how perhaps there's a hint there of them having the same facial features.
sentences.zh: 他留着长长的白头发，你知道的，它们匹配得相当好，你大概能看出其中似乎暗示着他们有着相同的面部特征。

sentences.en: And then finally, we have a theory that's been proposed by top symbologist Robert Langdon, and he proposes that the Mona Lisa is an androgynous fusion of the Egyptian god Amun.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们有一个由顶级符号学家罗伯特·兰登提出的理论，他提出《蒙娜丽莎》是埃及神明阿蒙的雌雄同体融合体，

sentences.en: So A-M-O-N, an anagram of Mona, and the goddess Isis, a.k.a.
sentences.zh: 也就是A-M-O-N，Mona的字母异序词，以及女神伊西斯，又名

sentences.en: Lisa.
sentences.zh: 丽莎。

sentences.en: So Mona Lisa, it's all there.
sentences.zh: 所以蒙娜丽莎，全都在这里了。

sentences.en: And Robert Langdon, of course, is the hero of Dan Brown's Da Vinci Code.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗伯特·兰登是丹·布朗的《达·芬奇密码》中的英雄。

sentences.en: And this is what Dan Brown has Langdon say.
sentences.zh: 这就是丹·布朗让兰登说的话。

sentences.en: Gentlemen, not only does the face of Mona Lisa look androgynous, but her name is an anagram of the divine union of male and female.
sentences.zh: 各位先生，蒙娜丽莎的脸不仅看起来雌雄同体，而且她的名字还是男性与女性神圣结合的字母异序词。

sentences.en: And that, my friends, is Da Vinci's little secret.
sentences.zh: 而这，我的朋友们，就是达·芬奇的小秘密。

sentences.en: Da Vinci again.
sentences.zh: 又是达·芬奇。

sentences.en: And the reason for Mona Lisa's knowing smile.
sentences.zh: 这也是蒙娜丽莎意味深长的微笑的原因。

sentences.en: Do you know who says this?
sentences.zh: 你知道是谁说的这话吗？

sentences.en: Tom Hanks.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·汉克斯。

sentences.en: Tom Hanks says it in the film, a person who's been on The Rest is History and had no shame about his involvement in that film.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·汉克斯在电影里说的，这个人曾上过《历史残余》播客节目，并且对参与那部电影毫不感到羞耻。

sentences.en: So, are you convinced by any of those?
sentences.zh: 那么，你被这些说法中的任何一个说服了吗？

sentences.en: No, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然没有。

sentences.en: I mean, I have to say, Tom, I think the way you've set it up suggests to me that it's none of these people, because you've said it with a degree of scepticism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，我不得不说，我觉得你铺垫的方式向我暗示这绝不是他们中的任何一个，因为你带着某种程度的怀疑态度说出了这些。

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely not that bloke who's a bloke.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，绝对不可能是那个本来就是个男的的家伙。

sentences.en: I think that's a definite no.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是否定的。

sentences.en: And I also don't think half of it is Leonardo da Vinci's face.
sentences.zh: 而且我也不认为其中有一半是列奥纳多·达·芬奇的脸。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, I will quote Donald Sassoon, who is the author of The Definitive History of the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 因此，我将引用唐纳德·萨苏恩的话，他是《蒙娜丽莎的权威历史》一书的作者。

sentences.en: I've drawn a lot on his book for this episode.

sentences.en: And at the end of his book, he declares himself agnostic as to who the painting portrays.

sentences.en: So, to quote him, my conclusion is that the evidence is too scanty for us to arrive at any firm identification.
sentences.zh: 引用他的话，我的结论是，证据太少，我们无法得出任何确切的身份认定。

sentences.en: We shall never know.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会知道。

sentences.en: Not that this will stop people from trying.

sentences.en: And of course, he's quite right.
sentences.zh: 当然，他是完全正确的。

sentences.en: People do continue to try.
sentences.zh: 人们确实还在不断尝试。

sentences.en: He then added this reflection.
sentences.zh: 他接着补充了这样一番感慨。

sentences.en: There is always the remote possibility that some new evidence will be unearthed.
sentences.zh: 总会有这样一种微小的可能性，即某些新的证据会被发掘出来。

sentences.en: And do you know, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，多米尼克？

sentences.en: Do you know, listeners?
sentences.zh: 听众朋友们，你们知道吗？

sentences.en: He was not wrong.
sentences.zh: 他并没有说错。

sentences.en: Because four years later, after Donald Sassoon wrote that in 2005, exactly such a piece of new evidence was unearthed.
sentences.zh: 因为在唐纳德·萨苏恩于2005年写下这句话的四年后，恰好出土了这样一条新证据。

sentences.en: And the brilliant thing about it, it conclusively proves who the woman portrayed in the Mona Lisa had been.
sentences.zh: 而最妙的是，它确凿地证明了《蒙娜丽莎》中所描绘的女人究竟是谁。

sentences.en: And more than that, it specifies pretty precisely exactly when Leonardo had begun painting it.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，它还相当精确地指明了列奥纳多究竟是什么时候开始绘制它的。
