sentences.en: Welcome back, everybody, to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎大家回到《历史残余》。

sentences.en: I am waiting with bated breath to find out who the Mona Lisa really was, and when the great painting was painted.
sentences.zh: 我正屏息以待，急切地想知道《蒙娜丽莎》的真正身份，以及这幅伟大的画作是何时创作的。

sentences.en: Tom, you promised us an absolute bombshell.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你向我们保证这是一个绝对的重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: I hope you're going to deliver.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能兑现承诺。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's go to the Florentine Chancellery in October 1503, where a clerk in the Chancellery is reading an edition of the letters of the great Roman orator Cicero.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回到1503年10月的佛罗伦萨大法官署，当时署里的一名书记员正在阅读伟大罗马演说家西塞罗的书信集。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Agostino Vespucci.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫阿戈斯蒂诺·韦斯普奇。

sentences.en: He's a very clever, very well-connected man.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常聪明、人脉很广的人。

sentences.en: So he's a humanist scholar.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一位人文主义学者。

sentences.en: And of course, humanist scholars, all they do at this point is read Cicero.
sentences.zh: 当然，人文主义学者在当时唯一做的事就是阅读西塞罗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's an assistant to Niccolò Machiavelli, famous author of political tratezes.
sentences.zh: 他是尼科洛·马基雅维利的助手，后者是著名的政治论著作家。

sentences.en: And he is a professional associate of Leonardo, because he's one of the administrators who just recently have signed a contract with Leonardo
sentences.zh: 他也是列奥纳多的职业合作伙伴，因为他是最近与列奥纳多签署合同的行政人员之一，

sentences.en: to paint the great council hall in Florence with a spectacular battle scene, an illustration of a great Florentine victory.
sentences.zh: 合同内容是为佛罗伦萨伟大议会大厅绘制一幅壮观的战争场景，以表现一场伟大的佛罗伦萨胜利的插图。

sentences.en: And as he's reading this book, this guy Vespucci comes across a reference in one of Cicero's letters to a famous Greek painter called Apelles.
sentences.zh: 正当他读这本书时，这个叫韦斯普奇的家伙在西塞罗的一封信中偶然看到了一处关于一位名叫阿佩莱斯的著名希腊画家的记载。

sentences.en: And Cicero describes Apelles as someone who had completed with the most polished art, the head and bust of Venus, but left the other part of her body inchoate.
sentences.zh: 西塞罗将阿佩莱斯描述为这样一个人：他以最精湛的艺术完成了维纳斯的头部和胸围，但却将她身体的其他部分留在了未完成的状态。

sentences.en: And Vespucci is very struck by this and he reaches for a pen and he makes a note in the margin and he writes, Apelles the painter.
sentences.zh: 韦斯普奇对此深有感触，他抓起一支笔，在空白处做了一个笔记，他写道：画家阿佩莱斯。

sentences.en: That is what Leonardo da Vinci does in all his pictures, as in the head of Lisa del Giacondo and Anne, the mother of Mary.
sentences.zh: 这正是列奥纳多·达·芬奇在他所有画作中所做的事情，比如丽莎·焦孔达的头像以及玛丽的母亲安妮的头像。

sentences.en: We will see what he will do in the hall of the great council, which he has now contracted to decorate.
sentences.zh: 我们将看看他在他现在承包装饰的大议会大厅里会怎么做。

sentences.en: And then he dates it 1503 October.
sentences.zh: 然后他标上了日期：1503年10月。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So a massive, massive bombshell.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其巨大的重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: Freud is wrong.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德错了。

sentences.en: Dr. Robert Langdon is wrong.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·兰登博士错了。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone who thought it wasn't the Mona Lisa is wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有认为画中人不是蒙娜丽莎的人都错了。

sentences.en: And so a huge shout out to Dr. Armin Schlechter, who is a librarian in the University Library in Heidelberg.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们要向海德堡大学图书馆的图书管理员阿明·施莱赫特博士致以崇高的敬意。

sentences.en: And he made the discovery in 2005.
sentences.zh: 他在2005年做出了这一发现。

sentences.en: And just to list what it proves, to make it clear,
sentences.zh: 为了让事情更清晰，让我们列举一下它证明了什么：

sentences.en: Vasari was absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 瓦萨里完全正确。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa is a portrait of Francesco del Giacondo's wife, Lisa Garrardini.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》弗朗切斯科·德尔·焦孔达的妻子丽莎·盖拉迪尼的肖像画。

sentences.en: Leonardo began the painting in 1503, which makes perfect sense, because as we said, in 1502, he'd been off in Rome working as chief engineer for Cesare Borgia.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多于1503年开始创作这幅画，这完全合情合理，因为正如我们所说，在1502年，他曾前往罗马担任切萨雷·博尔贾的首席工程师。

sentences.en: And in 1504, of course, he's going to start work on this great battle scene in the Florentine council hall.
sentences.zh: 当然，在1504年，他将开始创作佛罗伦萨议会大厅里这幅宏大的战争场景。

sentences.en: We also know that Lisa had just given birth to her second son.
sentences.zh: 我们还知道，丽莎刚刚生下了她的第二个儿子。

sentences.en: And so you can imagine that that might be a cause of celebration, something that her husband might want to mark by commissioning a portrait.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象这可能是一个值得庆祝的理由，她的丈夫可能会想通过定制一幅肖像画来纪念这件事。

sentences.en: And we can even work out who might have introduced Leonardo to Francesco, because Leonardo's father, Sir Piero, was Francesco's lawyer.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可以查明是谁把列奥纳多引见给弗朗切斯科的，因为列奥纳多的父亲皮耶罗先生是弗朗切斯科的律师。

sentences.en: And so I think that this clearly, in a sense, demythologizes the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，从某种意义上说，这清楚地去除了《蒙娜丽莎》身上的神秘色彩。

sentences.en: It's not a portrait of Leonardo in drag.
sentences.zh: 它不是女装大佬列奥纳多的肖像。

sentences.en: It's not his mother.
sentences.zh: 它也不是他的母亲。

sentences.en: It's not the sacred feminine.
sentences.zh: 这不是神圣女性的概念。

sentences.en: We can set the commissioning of the Mona Lisa absolutely in the context of daily life in Florence.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把《蒙娜丽莎》的创作完全置于当时佛罗伦萨的日常生活中。

sentences.en: These kind of networks of social relations that made the city run.
sentences.zh: 正是这种社会关系网络让这座城市运转起来。

sentences.en: You know, family proud businessmen, commissions, lawyers, all of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如自豪的商人家族、委托创作、律师，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So on one level, there's no mystery.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这并不神秘。

sentences.en: However.
sentences.zh: 然而。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are lots of questions, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 对，有很多问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, for example, if he did this as a commission,
sentences.zh: 因为，举个例子，如果这是受人委托创作的，

sentences.en: why does he not hand it over and get paid for it?
sentences.zh: 为什么他没有把画交出去并拿到报酬呢？

sentences.en: Why doesn't he give it to the Giacondo family?
sentences.zh: 为什么他不把它交给焦孔达家族？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that is a massive question.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，这绝对是一个巨大的疑问。

sentences.en: So, I mean, various answers to that question have been suggested.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，人们对这个问题提出了各种各样的答案。

sentences.en: Maybe the chance to use it as a calling card, as an advertisement for his talents.
sentences.zh: 也许这是把它当作一张名片、一个展示他才华的广告的机会。

sentences.en: It ends up being worth more to him than the fee he would have got from Francesco.
sentences.zh: 最终，这幅画对他的价值超过了他本来可以从弗朗切斯科那里得到的酬金。

sentences.en: Maybe he can't bear to finish it.
sentences.zh: 也许他是舍不得把它画完。

sentences.en: So Vasari, in his biography, says that Leonardo never finished it.
sentences.zh: 所以瓦萨里在他的传记中说，达芬奇从来没有完成过它。

sentences.en: Or maybe, you know, it does have some special meaning for him.
sentences.zh: 或者也许，你知道的，它对他来说确实有着某种特殊的意义。

sentences.en: Maybe he does see it as his great masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 也许他确实把它视为自己的伟大杰作。

sentences.en: Maybe he just can't bear to be separated from it.
sentences.zh: 也许他只是无法忍受与它分开。

sentences.en: And it's certainly the case that right from the beginning, it is viewed by everyone who sees it as a really revolutionary painting.
sentences.zh: 而且事实确实如此，从一开始，所有看到它的人都认为它是一幅真正具有革命性的画作。

sentences.en: So the pose of its sitter, the lifelike quality of the portrait, the mysterious quality of the landscape, all of this combines to make it seem to people who come and see it
sentences.zh: 所以，模特的姿态、肖像逼真的质感、风景神秘的意境，这一切结合起来，让前来观赏的人们觉得

sentences.en: really kind of thrilling, really innovative.
sentences.zh: 非常激动人心，极其富有创新精神。

sentences.en: So that really surprises me because as a Mona Lisa skeptic, as it were,
sentences.zh: 这真的让我很惊讶，因为作为一个“蒙娜丽莎”的怀疑论者，可以说是，

sentences.en: I'd always assumed that the aesthetic value of it was, as it were, projected onto it later.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为它的美学价值是后来才被赋予的，可以说是强加上去的。

sentences.en: Once it became famous, people said, oh, it's obviously brilliant, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 一旦它出了名，人们就会说，哦，它显然太棒了，等等等等。

sentences.en: But people probably didn't think it was brilliant at the time.
sentences.zh: 但当时的人们可能并不觉得它有多么了不起。

sentences.en: But you're telling me that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 但你却告诉我这是错的。

sentences.en: And even at the time, for example, other Renaissance painters thought this is special.
sentences.zh: 甚至在当时，比如其他文艺复兴时期的画家也认为这幅画很特别。

sentences.en: So Raphael is in Florence at the time when Leonardo is painting it.
sentences.zh: 达芬奇作画时，拉斐尔正好在佛罗伦萨。

sentences.en: He comes and sees it and he's blown away by it.
sentences.zh: 他来看了这幅画，并且被深深地震撼了。

sentences.en: And it's patently a massive influence on Raphael's painting.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这给拉斐尔的绘画带来了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And this distinctive pose that the Mona Lisa has, it's very widely copied, so much so that that pose comes to be called the Gioconda.
sentences.zh: 而且《蒙娜丽莎》这种独特的姿态被广泛模仿，以至于这种姿态后来被称为“焦孔达”式。

sentences.en: So it's that famous.
sentences.zh: 可见它当时有多么出名。

sentences.en: And by the end of his life, Leonardo has become a tourist attraction in his own right.
sentences.zh: 到他生命快结束时，达芬奇本身就已经成了一个旅游景点。

sentences.en: And having the chance to see the Mona Lisa is a part of the package.
sentences.zh: 有机会去看《蒙娜丽莎》成了其中的配套项目之一。

sentences.en: When people come and visit Leonardo, they want to see this painting.
sentences.zh: 当人们来拜访达芬奇时，他们都想看看这幅画。

sentences.en: Now, when Leonardo dies, he's not actually in Florence.
sentences.zh: 然而，达芬奇去世时并不在佛罗伦萨。

sentences.en: He's not even in Italy.
sentences.zh: 他甚至不在意大利。

sentences.en: He is in France at Amboise on the Loire.
sentences.zh: 他在法国卢瓦尔河畔昂布瓦斯。

sentences.en: He dies there on the 2nd of May, 1519.
sentences.zh: 他在那里离世，时间是1519年5月2日。

sentences.en: And the story is that he dies in the arms of the French king, François Premier, Francis I, because Leonardo had gone to the court of Francis I in 1516.
sentences.zh: 传说他是死在法国国王弗朗瓦一世（François Premier, Francis I）的怀里，因为达芬奇在1516年应邀来到了弗朗索瓦一世的宫廷。

sentences.en: And he goes there partly because there are just no patrons worthy of his status who are willing to employ him in Italy.
sentences.zh: 他去那里，一部分原因是在意大利已经找不到任何配得上他身份、愿意雇用他的赞助人了。

sentences.en: And partly because Francis I really, really wants him and is willing to pay anything.
sentences.zh: 另一部分原因则是弗朗索瓦一世实在太渴望得到他，并且愿意付出任何代价。

sentences.en: And it actually reminds me a bit of the way in which Mohammed bin Salman, the strong man of
sentences.zh: 这其实让我想起了穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼，这位

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia, paid an obscene amount of money for the Salvata Mundi, this painting that has been attributed to Leonardo.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯的强人，曾花了一笔天价买下《救世主》，这幅被认为是达芬奇作品的画作。

sentences.en: There are plenty of people who think it isn't a Leonardo, but it's now gone to Saudi Arabia rather in the way that Leonardo went to the court of Francis I.
sentences.zh: 尽管有很多人认为它并非出自达芬奇之手，但它如今还是去了沙特阿拉伯，就像当年达芬奇前往弗朗索瓦一世的宫廷一样。

sentences.en: And when Leonardo dies, Francis I makes sure to buy the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 达芬奇逝世后，弗朗索瓦一世确保买下了《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: And the result of this is that the painting is going to end up becoming part of the cultural patrimony, not of Italy, but of France.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，这幅画最终成为了文化遗产的一部分，不属于意大利，而是属于法国。

sentences.en: And this is crucial for its future history.
sentences.zh: 这对其未来的历史至关重要。

sentences.en: So it's become part of French tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以它已经成为了法国传统的一部分。

sentences.en: But in the next couple of centuries, the French don't make a huge amount of it, do they?
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的两百年里，法国人并没有太把这幅画当回事，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, for example, in 1625, Louis XIII actually gives it away.
sentences.zh: 比如，在1625年，路易十三甚至把它送人了。

sentences.en: Well, he agrees to give it away to the Duke of Buckingham with his famously long legs, great favourites of James I.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他同意把它送给白金汉公爵，这位公爵以长腿闻名，深受詹姆斯一世的喜爱。

sentences.en: Basically, Buckingham's going to give him a Holbein and, I think, a Titian.
sentences.zh: 基本上，白金汉打算回赠他一幅小荷尔拜因，以及一幅提香的作品，我想是的。

sentences.en: And it's actually Louis's courtiers who say, hold on, this is actually quite a good painting.
sentences.zh: 实际上是路易的朝臣们说，等等，这其实是一幅相当不错的画。

sentences.en: Don't give it away.
sentences.zh: 别把它送人。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's such a shame because the Mona Lisa could have ended up in London.
sentences.zh: 对啊，太遗憾了，因为《蒙娜丽莎》本来可能会流落到伦敦。

sentences.en: See, I think if it had ended up in London, maybe it wouldn't have been such a big deal.
sentences.zh: 你看，我觉得如果它最终到了伦敦，也许就不会引起这么大的轰动了。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我想你完全说对了。

sentences.en: That kind of for two centuries after Leonardo's death, the painting does go into eclipse.
sentences.zh: 在达芬奇死后的那两百年里，这幅画确实陷入了籍籍无名的境地。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's not showcased.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，它没有被拿出来展示。

sentences.en: It's not a great treasure of the French king.
sentences.zh: 它不是法国国王的顶级珍宝。

sentences.en: In 1695, it gets moved to Versailles, but it's put in a pretty obscure corridor.
sentences.zh: 1695年，它被移到了凡尔赛宫，但被安置在一条相当偏僻的走廊里。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not something that most people would notice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是大多数人会注意到的东西。

sentences.en: And then in 1750, there's a very clear demonstration of how the Mona Lisa is rated.
sentences.zh: 然后在1750年，发生了一件能非常清楚地反映出《蒙娜丽莎》当时地位的事。

sentences.en: Because 110 of the best paintings in the Royal Collection at Versailles are put on display at the Palais de Luxembourg in Paris for the delectation of invited visitors.
sentences.zh: 因为凡尔赛宫皇家收藏中最好的110幅画作被陈列在巴黎的卢森堡宫，供受邀的访客们欣赏。

sentences.en: So 110 paintings.
sentences.zh: 总共是110幅画。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa is not one of those 110 paintings.
sentences.zh: 而《蒙娜丽莎》并不在这110幅画中。

sentences.en: So it's not even top 100.
sentences.zh: 所以它连前100名都没进。

sentences.en: So that complicates things because you said right at the beginning, oh, people thought it was amazing right from the start.
sentences.zh: 这就让事情变得复杂了，因为你一开始就说，哦，人们从一开始就觉得它太惊艳了。

sentences.en: But obviously now there's a period where people don't think it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 但显然现在出现了一个人们并不觉得它惊艳的时期。

sentences.en: And something changes, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 情况发生了变化，对吧？

sentences.en: That is because Renaissance painting goes out of fashion.
sentences.zh: 那是因为文艺复兴时期的绘画过时了。

sentences.en: There isn't a category of Renaissance painting at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时根本没有“文艺复兴时期绘画”这一门类。

sentences.en: And Leonardo's luster has dimmed.
sentences.zh: 而且达芬奇的光芒也黯淡了。

sentences.en: The posthumous reputation of Leonardo is also bound up with the kind of the decline in the value of the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 达芬奇死后的声誉也与《蒙娜丽莎》价值的下降紧密相连。

sentences.en: So what's changed?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么改变了？

sentences.en: What changes and when?
sentences.zh: 是什么在改变，又是在什么时候改变的？

sentences.en: Is it the wake of the French Revolution?
sentences.zh: 是在法国大革命之后吗？

sentences.en: It's always the French Revolution, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 总归是法国大革命，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, French Revolution is crucial because, of course, suddenly, you know, these paintings are not stuffed away in a royal palace.
sentences.zh: 没错，法国大革命至关重要，因为当然了，突然之间，这些画不再被塞在皇宫的角落里了。

sentences.en: They are being brought out for the people to admire and enjoy.
sentences.zh: 它们被拿出来供人们欣赏和赞叹。

sentences.en: And the revolutionaries set up a great new museum in the Louvre and the Mona Lisa is moved there.
sentences.zh: 革命者在卢浮宫建立了一座宏伟的新博物馆，《蒙娜丽莎》就被搬到了那里。

sentences.en: It is briefly transferred to Napoleon's bedroom, along with a load of other paintings.
sentences.zh: 它曾短暂地被转移到拿破仑的卧室里，同行的还有一大堆其他的画作。

sentences.en: So it's in Napoleon's bedroom from 1800 up to when he becomes emperor in 1804.
sentences.zh: 所以从1800年到1804年他称帝期间，它一直挂在拿破仑的卧室里。

sentences.en: And the Mona Lisa then goes back to the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 之后，《蒙娜丽莎》又回到了卢浮宫。

sentences.en: And from that point on, the Mona Lisa is on public display in the world's largest and most prestigious museum.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，《蒙娜丽莎》开始在世界上最大、最负盛名的博物馆里公开长期展出。

sentences.en: You know, Paris is the acknowledged capital of European high culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，巴黎是公認的欧洲高级文化之都。

sentences.en: And so it's in the right place now for it to start ascending the list to go up, you know, towards the kind of the top of the pops.
sentences.zh: 所以它现在处于正确的位置，开始在榜单上攀升，你知道的，朝着最热门的巅峰迈进。

sentences.en: But slower process than you would think.
sentences.zh: 但这个过程比你想象的要慢。

sentences.en: So in 1852, there was a list drawn up, a sort of estimate of all the artworks in the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 所以在1852年，曾拟定过一份清单，大致评估了卢浮宫里所有的艺术品。

sentences.en: And they ranked their value, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 他们对这些艺术品的价值进行了排名，不是吗？

sentences.en: And the Mona Lisa was ranked at 90,000 francs.
sentences.zh: 当时《蒙娜丽莎》的估价是9万法郎。

sentences.en: But there's a painting by Titian at 150,000.
sentences.zh: 但有一幅提香的作品值15万法郎。

sentences.en: There's one by Raphael at 400,000 francs.
sentences.zh: 有一幅拉斐尔的作品值40万法郎。

sentences.en: Another Raphael at 600,000 francs.
sentences.zh: 另一幅拉斐尔的作品则值60万法郎。

sentences.en: So by those criteria, the Mona Lisa is still relatively a minnow.
sentences.zh: 所以按这些标准来看，《蒙娜丽莎》当时仍然相对算个小角色。

sentences.en: But then progressively over the course of the 19th century, the Mona Lisa starts to benefit from really quite profound changes in cultural and intellectual tastes.
sentences.zh: 但随后在整个19世纪的过程中，《蒙娜丽莎》开始受益于文化和知识品味方面相当深远的变化。

sentences.en: And I guess that the most influential of those is romanticism.
sentences.zh: 我猜其中影响最深远的当属浪漫主义。

sentences.en: You know, it's a very broad brush word, but let's use it as a shorthand.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一个非常泛泛的词，但我们就把它当作一个简化的代称吧。

sentences.en: So it's shorthand for the worship of genius, admiration for works of art that have a sense of mystery, perhaps of incompletion about them.
sentences.zh: 所以它是崇拜天才、赞美那些带有一点神秘感甚至未完成感的艺术品的代名词。

sentences.en: And, of course, a fascination with wild and sublime landscapes.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有对狂野壮丽风景的迷恋。

sentences.en: Romantics love a wild and sublime landscape.
sentences.zh: 浪漫主义者酷爱狂野而壮丽的风景。

sentences.en: And all of this massively helps to inflate the reputation of Leonardo, who, over the course of the 19th century, starts to be seen as not just a genius, but the supreme genius of,
sentences.zh: 所有这些都極大地抬高了达芬奇的声誉。在整个19世纪期间，他开始被视为不仅仅是一个天才，而是终极天才，也就是

sentences.en: as we will see, what comes to be called the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将会看到的，后来被称为“文艺复兴”的时代中的至高天才。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is precisely the range of things that he does.
sentences.zh: 原因正是在于他涉猎的领域之广。

sentences.en: You know, he's a painter.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是个画家。

sentences.en: He leaves lots of his paintings unfinished.
sentences.zh: 他留下了许多未完成的画作。

sentences.en: Romantics love that.
sentences.zh: 浪漫主义者对这一套爱不释手。

sentences.en: But he's also someone who's interested in mountains and tanks and fetuses and swans and eyeballs and everything, just everything.
sentences.zh: 但他也是一个对高山、坦克、胎儿、天鹅、眼球以及世间万物都感兴趣的人，几乎是无所不包。

sentences.en: And so, you know, romantics love that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，浪漫主义者太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: And so he comes to be seen as a universal genius.
sentences.zh: 因此，他开始被视为一个全能天才。

sentences.en: And if he's a universal genius, then what can the Mona Lisa be but a universal woman?
sentences.zh: 既然他是个全能天才，那么《蒙娜丽莎》除了是一位全能女性之外，还能是什么呢？

sentences.en: So, in other words, the fating of Leonardo,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，对达芬奇的追捧，

sentences.en: the establishment of Leonardo as the archetype of a great genius is the absolutely necessary precondition for the fating of the Mona Lisa as the greatest painting of all time.
sentences.zh: 将达芬奇确立为伟大天才的绝对原型，是把《蒙娜丽莎》捧为有史以来最伟大画作的绝对必要前提。

sentences.en: So to quote Donald Sassoon, the Mona Lisa acquired its special status because of its association with Leonardo, not the other way round.
sentences.zh: 用唐纳德·萨松的话来说，《蒙娜丽莎》之所以获得特殊的地位，是因为它与达芬奇的联系，而不是反过来。

sentences.en: So I think Leonardo as supreme genius, that is one crucial influence on the inflation of the Mona Lisa's reputation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，达芬奇作为至高无上的天才，是推高《蒙娜丽莎》声誉的关键影响因素之一。

sentences.en: The other one, and this is what Walter Pater is all about, romantics have a massive thing for predatory females, for femme fatale, as they come to be called.
sentences.zh: 另一个因素，这也是沃尔特·佩特所强调的，浪漫主义者对掠夺成性的女性、也就是后来所谓的蛇蝎美人（femme fatale）有着极大的狂热。

sentences.en: And there's a brilliant book, which was published way back in 1933, which covers this.
sentences.zh: 有一本很棒的书早在1933年就出版了，探讨的就是这个主题。

sentences.en: It's called The Romantic Agony, translated into English.
sentences.zh: 它被翻译成英文，书名叫《浪漫主义的痛苦》。

sentences.en: It's by an Italian critic called Mario Praz.
sentences.zh: 作者是一位名叫马里奥·普拉茨的意大利评论家。

sentences.en: And he writes brilliantly about how over the course of the 19th century, male artists and writers become obsessed with a very distinctive vision of female beauty.
sentences.zh: 他在书中极佳地论述了在19世纪期间，男性艺术家和作家如何痴迷于一种非常独特的女性美学视角。

sentences.en: And to quote Praz, tainted with pain, corruption and death.
sentences.zh: 引用普拉茨的话，“沾染着痛苦、腐败与死亡”。

sentences.en: And Praz writes about how by the end of the 19th century, this beauty had become illumined with the smile of the geoconda.
sentences.zh: 普拉茨写道，到19世纪末，这种美已经“被焦孔达的微笑所照亮”。

sentences.en: And this is where Walter Pater comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是沃尔特·佩特登场的地方。

sentences.en: He's a massive, massive influence on the English speaking world.
sentences.zh: 他对英语世界产生了巨大无比的影响。

sentences.en: That passage that you read, I mean, it may seem kind of, you know, purple to us,
sentences.zh: 你刚才读的那段文字，我的意思是，对我们来说可能显得有点过分华丽，

sentences.en: but it determines how people in the English speaking world see the Mona Lisa for generations and generations.
sentences.zh: 但它决定了世世代代的英语世界人们看待《蒙娜丽莎》的方式。

sentences.en: But the guys who really go big on this, unsurprisingly, since they own it, are the French.
sentences.zh: 但真正对此大肆渲染的，不出所料，正是拥有这幅画的法国人。

sentences.en: So I'll cite two writers in particular.
sentences.zh: 所以我特别要举出两位作家。

sentences.en: And the first is Théophile Gautier, who was a poet, a novelist, a critic.
sentences.zh: 第一位是泰奥菲尔·戈蒂埃，他是一位诗人、小说家兼评论家。

sentences.en: And he is the guy who, before Pater, establishes Mona Lisa as not just as an archetype of beauty, but as an eternal archetype of beauty.
sentences.zh: 正是他在佩特之前，将《蒙娜丽莎》确立为不仅是美的原型，更是永恒美的原型。

sentences.en: Someone who has essentially existed since the beginning of time.
sentences.zh: 一个本质上从时间的开端就存在的人。

sentences.en: She's older than Egypt.
sentences.zh: 她比埃及更古老。

sentences.en: She's older than Greece, older than Rome.
sentences.zh: 她比希腊更古老，比罗马更古老。

sentences.en: So to quote Gautier, she is always there smiling with sensuality, mocking her numerous lovers.
sentences.zh: 引用戈蒂埃的话，她永远坐在那里，带着感官的微笑，嘲弄着她无数的追求者。

sentences.en: So a bit like Cleopatra there, who Cleopatra was supposed to sleep with men and then kill them.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像克利奥帕特拉，传说克利奥帕特拉会与男人们同床共枕然后杀掉他们。

sentences.en: She has the serene countenance of a woman, sure that she will remain beautiful forever and certain to be greater than the ideal of poets and artists.
sentences.zh: 她拥有女性宁静的面容，确信自己将永远美丽，并注定要超越诗人和艺术家心中的理想。

sentences.en: So again, perhaps the hint there of the vampire, someone who is always beautiful, feeding off the blood of her prey.
sentences.zh: 所以这里再次隐约暗示了吸血鬼的形象，一个永远美丽、靠猎物的鲜血为生的人。

sentences.en: People are projecting an awful lot onto Mona Lisa, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 人们在《蒙娜丽莎》身上寄托了太多的情感和解读，不是吗？

sentences.en: But I mean, another example, the historian Jules Michelet, who wrote an enormous history of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，另一个例子是历史学家朱尔·米什莱，他写了一部宏大的法国大革命史。

sentences.en: The first historian to use the word Renaissance, by the way, or at least to take it back up from Vasari and to popularize it.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他是第一位使用“文艺复兴”这个词的历史学家，或者至少是从瓦萨里那里重新拾起并将其普及开来。

sentences.en: And Michelet goes even further, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而米什莱走得更远，对吧？

sentences.en: He basically says, you know, the Mona Lisa is a dominatrix.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，你知道的，《蒙娜丽莎》就是一个施虐癖女王。

sentences.en: Is that too strong, a dominatrix?
sentences.zh: 这个词会不会太重了，施虐癖女王？

sentences.en: Well, you can read what he said about her.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以读读他是怎么评价她的。

sentences.en: This canvas attracts me, revolts me, consumes me, and I go to her in spite of myself as the bird to the snake.
sentences.zh: 这块画布吸引我、抗拒我、吞噬我，我不由自主地走向她，就像飞鸟扑向毒蛇。

sentences.en: But you can see, I mean, this is all kind of very exciting for people in Victorian parlours reading this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看出，我的意思是，对于维多利亚时代的沙龙里阅读这类东西的人来说，这一切都非常刺激。

sentences.en: And of course, as the 19th century goes on towards the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 当然，随着19世纪向20世纪迈进，

sentences.en: photography for the first time is starting to be equal to the challenge of capturing the image of the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 摄影技术首次开始能够胜任捕捉《蒙娜丽莎》影像的挑战。

sentences.en: So by the end of the 19th century, you've got all this purple prose about vampires and snakes and things.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪末，你会看到各种关于吸血鬼、蛇之类事物的华丽辞藻。

sentences.en: And for the first time, you have images of the Mona Lisa that are very easy to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上第一次，人们可以非常容易地复制出《蒙娜丽莎》的图像。

sentences.en: And so people can actually look at it without having to go to the Louvre and kind of see it in the flesh, as it were.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们无需亲自前往卢浮宫，就能看到它，可以说是大饱眼福。

sentences.en: And I would say that by the beginning of the 20th century, the Mona Lisa is probably the most famous painting in the Louvre, probably one of the most famous paintings in the world.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，到20世纪初，《蒙娜丽莎》大概已经是卢浮宫里最著名的画作，也可能是世界上最著名的画作之一。

sentences.en: It's kind of had a very meteoric rise.
sentences.zh: 它的崛起可以说是非常神速。

sentences.en: But there's one final thing that's needed to complete its ascent to the absolute top of the echelon.
sentences.zh: 但要完成它向绝对巅峰阶层的跃升，还缺少最后一步。

sentences.en: And this happens on the 21st of August, 1911.
sentences.zh: 这件事发生在1911年8月21日。

sentences.en: And what happens puts the Mona Lisa on the front page of newspapers around the world.
sentences.zh: 而发生的事情让《蒙娜丽莎》登上了世界各地报纸的头版。

sentences.en: So 21st of August, 1911.
It's a Monday and the Louvre is shut for cleaning.
sentences.zh: 那天是星期一，卢浮宫闭馆进行清洁。

sentences.en: While it's shut, people walk through the room in which the Mona Lisa is kept and they find that it's gone.
sentences.zh: 在闭馆期间，人们走过存放《蒙娜丽莎》的房间，发现它不见了。

sentences.en: There is only the empty frame in which it had been contained and there is complete outrage.
sentences.zh: 那里只剩下一个空画框，人们对此感到无比愤怒。

sentences.en: The director of France's museums is sacked.
sentences.zh: 法国博物馆的馆长被解雇了。

sentences.en: The Petit Parisien, which at the time was the world's largest circulation newspaper,
sentences.zh: 当时世界上发行量最大的报纸《小巴黎人报》

sentences.en: splashed the painting on the front page together with the brilliantly caustic comment.
sentences.zh: 在头版刊登了这幅画，并配上了一句极其辛辣讽刺的评论。

sentences.en: Well, at least we still have the frame.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少我们还留着画框。

sentences.en: The news goes around Paris, around France, around the world.
sentences.zh: 这个消息传遍了巴黎、法国乃至全世界。

sentences.en: Huge crowds kind of descend on the Louvre, go to look at where the painting had been.
sentences.zh: 大批人潮涌向卢浮宫，去看这幅画曾经悬挂的地方。

sentences.en: Much larger crowds than had ever assembled when the Mona Lisa was actually in situ.
sentences.zh: 聚集的人群比《蒙娜丽莎》还在馆内时任何时候都要多得多。

sentences.en: And there's a desperate kind of Inspector Clouseau type pursuit of the painting, which is always raking up ludicrous suspects.
sentences.zh: 人们对这幅画展开了像笨拙的克鲁索探长一样的绝望追查，总能翻出一些荒谬的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: So one of them is the famous poet Guillaume Apollinaire, who is arrested.
sentences.zh: 其中一位就是著名的诗人纪尧姆·阿波利奈尔，他被捕了。

sentences.en: And Apollinaire and a friend of his, who is an up-and-coming Spanish painter resident in Paris at the time, called Pablo Picasso, actually end up on trial.
sentences.zh: 而阿波利奈尔和他的一个朋友——当时住在巴黎、崭露头角的西班牙画家巴勃罗·毕加索——最终双双受审。

sentences.en: Both Apollinaire and Picasso are acquitted.
sentences.zh: 阿波利奈尔和毕加索都被无罪释放了。

sentences.en: It's a suggestion of how this crime is not only inflating the reputation of the Mona Lisa,
sentences.zh: 这表明，这起犯罪不仅提升了《蒙娜丽莎》的声誉，

sentences.en: but is also kind of rubbing up against artists and poets and painters who are the cutting edge of the avant-garde,
sentences.zh: 而且还与那些处于前卫艺术尖端的艺术家、诗人和画家产生了某种交集，

sentences.en: which I think is another part of why the Mona Lisa suddenly comes to seem much more interesting to people than it had previously done.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是为什么《蒙娜丽莎》突然让人觉得比以往任何时候都更有趣的另一个原因。

sentences.en: However, the police seem helpless.
sentences.zh: 然而，警方似乎束手无策。

sentences.en: A year passes.
sentences.zh: 一年过去了。

sentences.en: There are no leads.
sentences.zh: 没有任何线索。

sentences.en: And by 1913, so that's a couple of years after the theft, the Mona Lisa is removed from the catalogue of the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 到了1913年，也就是失窃几年后，《蒙娜丽莎》从卢浮宫的藏品目录中被除名了。

sentences.en: It's basically an admission of defeat.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是承认失败。

sentences.en: You know, this painting is gone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这幅画不见了。

sentences.en: We're never going to get it back.
sentences.zh: 我们再也找不回它了。

sentences.en: But then, as dramatically as it had vanished, the Mona Lisa reappears.
sentences.zh: 但随后，《蒙娜丽莎》像它消失时一样戏剧性地重新出现了。

sentences.en: And it reappears because in Florence, where, of course, the Mona Lisa had originally been painted,
sentences.zh: 之所以重新出现，是因为在佛罗伦萨——当然，《蒙娜丽莎》最初正是在那里创作的——

sentences.en: an antique dealer called Alfredo Geri gets a letter which has been signed Leonardo.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫阿尔弗雷多·杰里的古董商收到了一封署名莱昂纳多的信。

sentences.en: And in this letter, Leonardo says that he wants to hand over the Mona Lisa to the Offizzi, the great gallery in Florence.
sentences.zh: 在这封信中，莱昂纳多表示他想把《蒙娜丽莎》交还给佛罗伦萨伟大的乌菲兹美术馆。

sentences.en: And he hints that he wants to do this for patriotic reasons.
sentences.zh: 他暗示他出于爱国主义原因才想这么做。

sentences.en: He does also say that he wants 500,000 lira to cover his expenses.
sentences.zh: 他还确实说过，他想要50万里拉来弥补他的开销。

sentences.en: But he's going very big on the fact that he's Italian and he's doing this for patriotic reasons.
sentences.zh: 但他极力强调自己是个意大利人，这么做是出于爱国主义原因。

sentences.en: So the antique dealer arranges to meet him.
sentences.zh: 于是这位古董商安排与他会面。

sentences.en: And Leonardo, Julie arrives from Paris.
sentences.zh: 莱昂纳多准时从巴黎赶来。

sentences.en: And Gerry and the head curator from the Offizzi ask to see the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 杰里和乌菲兹美术馆的首席馆长要求查看《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: He kind of pulls the Mona Lisa out from his suitcase, unwraps it.
sentences.zh: 他从手提箱里把《蒙娜丽莎》拉出来，解开了包装。

sentences.en: The head curator of the Offizzi inspects it.
sentences.zh: 乌菲兹美术馆的首席馆长进行了检查。

sentences.en: It's clear it is indeed the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这确实是《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: And so they have the thief arrested.
sentences.zh: 于是他们让人把小偷逮捕了。

sentences.en: And he turns out to be a guy called Vincenzo Perugia.
sentences.zh: 结果证明他是一个名叫温琴佐·佩鲁贾的家伙。

sentences.en: And he was an Italian painter-decorator who had been working in the Louvre, painting the walls on the fateful Monday that the painting was stolen.
sentences.zh: 他是一名意大利油漆工兼装饰工，曾在卢浮宫工作，在画作失窃那个命运般的星期一负责粉刷墙壁。

sentences.en: And he seized his chance.
sentences.zh: 他抓住了这个机会。

sentences.en: And he just lifted it out from his frame, hidden it under his coat, walked off across the courtyard of the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 他只是把它从画框里取出来，藏在大衣底下，穿过了卢浮宫的庭院。

sentences.en: He kind of waved at a guard and gone out through the door.
sentences.zh: 他朝警卫挥了挥手，从门口走了出去。

sentences.en: And that was that.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And he kept it for a year and a half hidden under his bed.
sentences.zh: 他把它藏在床底下藏了一年半。

sentences.en: And, you know, his motivation, which he holds to throughout his subsequent trial, is that he was outraged that the Mona Lisa was in Paris.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他一直坚持到随后的审判中的动机是，他对《蒙娜丽莎》在巴黎感到愤怒。

sentences.en: He thought it should be in Florence.
sentences.zh: 他认为它应该在佛罗伦萨。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons why he's so outraged is he thought that Napoleon had stolen it from the Offizzi.
sentences.zh: 他之所以如此愤怒，原因之一是他以为拿破仑是从乌菲兹美术馆把它偷走的。

sentences.en: So this was his motivation.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的动机。

sentences.en: And there's no reason to doubt that he was genuinely suffused with kind of nationalist enthusiasm, is there?
sentences.zh: 没有任何理由怀疑他内心确实充满了某种民族主义热情，不是吗？

sentences.en: The problem is he turns out to be really boring.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他这个人无聊透顶。

sentences.en: You know, people had wanted a master criminal, a kind of gentleman cracksman.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们原本想要一个江洋大盗，一个温文尔雅的神偷。

sentences.en: And he's not at all.
sentences.zh: 而他一点也不符合。

sentences.en: And because he does not become the focus of media attention, which he might otherwise have done, instead, the star is Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 正因为他没有像原本可能的那样成为媒体关注的焦点，相反，明星成了《蒙娜丽莎》本身。

sentences.en: And what previously the painting had been called It, it's from this point on that the Mona Lisa starts to be feminized.
sentences.zh: 以前这幅画被称为“它”，正是从这个时候起，《蒙娜丽莎》开始被赋予女性色彩。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa is she.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》变成了“她”。

sentences.en: She is coming back to Paris.
sentences.zh: 她要回到巴黎了。

sentences.en: She is returning to the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 她正在重返卢浮宫。

sentences.en: She is being put back in her frame.
sentences.zh: 她被重新安放回了画框里。

sentences.en: And when she is put back in her frame in the Louvre, she sits from that point on as the absolute symbol, the absolute embodiment of high art, of high culture,
sentences.zh: 当她被放回卢浮宫的画框中时，从那时起，她就作为高级艺术、高级文化的绝对象征、绝对化身而端坐着，

sentences.en: with capital letters, both of them in capital letters.
sentences.zh: 这两个词都有大写字母，都是大写字母。

sentences.en: And from that point on, the reputation of the Mona Lisa as the embodiment of the Renaissance, of Western art, of art full stop, is absolutely secure.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，《蒙娜丽莎》作为文艺复兴、西方艺术乃至艺术本身的化身的声誉就绝对稳固了。

sentences.en: Although it does have the kind of paradoxical effect that now the Mona Lisa is the icon of high art.
sentences.zh: 尽管它确实带来了一种悖论似的影响，那就是现在《蒙娜丽莎》成为了高级艺术的偶像。

sentences.en: Of course, enthusiasts of high art start to turn against it and to say, oh, it's a bit vulgar.
sentences.zh: 当然，高级艺术的爱好者们开始反对它，说，哦，这有点庸俗。

sentences.en: It's a bit trashy.
sentences.zh: 这有点俗气。

sentences.en: She becomes the embodiment of middle brow art enthusiasm, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 她成了中产阶级艺术热情的化身，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, isn't that the, you know, somebody, if you're a student and you go in and somebody's got a print of the Mona Lisa on their wall,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道不是吗？如果你是个学生，你走进别人的房间，看到墙上挂着一张《蒙娜丽莎》的印刷品，

sentences.en: you kind of think you don't really know much about art.
sentences.zh: 你就会觉得这个人其实对艺术一无所知。

sentences.en: Do you not think?
sentences.zh: 难道你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a classic FM of art.
sentences.zh: 是的，它是艺术界里的古典音乐电台。

sentences.en: But this in turn, of course, I mean, only fuels her further ascent into the stratosphere of fame.
sentences.zh: 当然，这反过来又进一步助长了她向名望平流层的冲刺。

sentences.en: And you can see it operating in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它在各种方面发挥着作用。

sentences.en: So because she's famous, because people are meant to take her seriously and kind of offer her obeisance, of course, she starts to be parodied.
sentences.zh: 所以，因为她很有名，因为人们理应认真对待她并向她顶礼膜拜，理所当然地，她开始被恶搞。

sentences.en: And the most famous of these parodies is done in 1919.
sentences.zh: 其中最著名的恶搞完成于1919年。

sentences.en: So only, you know, a few years after her abduction and return.
sentences.zh: 也就是在她被劫持并归还仅仅几年之后。

sentences.en: And this is done by the artist Marcel Duchamp, who's also very keen on urinals.
sentences.zh: 这是由艺术家马塞尔·杜尚完成的，他对小便池也情有独钟。

sentences.en: And he gets a postcard of the Mona Lisa and he draws a moustache and a goatee on it.
sentences.zh: 他弄到了一张《蒙娜丽莎》的明信片，并在上面画了一撮小胡子和山羊胡。

sentences.en: And he calls it in English, uses the letters L-H-O-O-Q.
sentences.zh: 他用英文给它命名，使用了L-H-O-O-Q这几个字母。

sentences.en: But Dominic, with your mastery of French, do you want to just explain to people what that means in French?
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，凭借你对法语的精通，你想给大伙儿解释一下这在法语里是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: It's a tremendous example of French humour.
sentences.zh: 这是一个法国幽默的绝佳例子。

sentences.en: L-H-O-O-Q in French is L-H-O-O-Q, which means she is, basically, she's hot in the arse.
sentences.zh: 法语里的L-H-O-O-Q听起来就像“她身材火辣”，基本上就是说她屁股很性感。

sentences.en: She's hot in the bind.
sentences.zh: 她屁股很辣。

sentences.en: So tremendous banter there from Marcel Duchamp.
sentences.zh: 马塞尔·杜尚真是开了个绝妙的玩笑。

sentences.en: Outrage and consternation.
sentences.zh: 一片哗然与惊恐。

sentences.en: And of course, the scandal just further amplifies the Mona Lisa's fame.
sentences.zh: 当然，丑闻进一步放大了《蒙娜丽莎》的名气。

sentences.en: Then, of course, there's mass reproduction.
sentences.zh: 接着，当然就是大规模复制。

sentences.en: So the more scope for reproducing the Mona Lisa, the more she's reproduced.
sentences.zh: 所以复制《蒙娜丽莎》的空间越大，她被复制得就越多。

sentences.en: And it's really telling that in 1963, she is the first painting to be reproduced by Andy Warhol.
sentences.zh: 1963年，她成为第一幅被安迪·沃霍尔复制的画作，这非常说明问题。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the true measure of fame.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是名气的真正衡量标准。

sentences.en: And Warhol had been inspired to do it by the fact that in 1963, the Mona Lisa had come to America, a kind of diplomatic gift from De Gaulle to Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 沃霍尔之所以受到启发，是因为1963年《蒙娜丽莎》来到了美国，这是戴高乐送给肯尼迪的一份外交礼物。

sentences.en: And so that makes the Mona Lisa even more famous in America.
sentences.zh: 这使得《蒙娜丽莎》在美国更加名声大噪。

sentences.en: Then in 1974, it visits Japan.
sentences.zh: 然后在1974年，它访问了日本。

sentences.en: And that kind of lights the fuse on Japanese enthusiasm for going to the Louvre and taking photographs of the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 这仿佛点燃了日本公众前往卢浮宫参观并拍摄《蒙娜丽莎》的热情导火索。

sentences.en: And I would say that it's not an exaggeration that now the Mona Lisa ranks not just as the archetype of high art, but kind of as the ultimate global icon of tourism.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，毫不夸张地说，现在《蒙娜丽莎》不仅跻身于高级艺术的原型，更是成为了旅游业的终极全球偶像。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the one object in the world, probably, that tourists, the mass of tourists, want to see more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它可能是世界上唯一一件让广大游客最想一睹为快的物件。

sentences.en: I mean, it is the single most popular object held by any museum in the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是世界上任何博物馆拥有的最受欢迎的单一藏品。

sentences.en: And the Louvre is the most visited museum.
sentences.zh: 卢浮宫是参观人数最多的博物馆。

sentences.en: You have nine million people going there a year.
sentences.zh: 每年有九百万人去那里参观。

sentences.en: And I think according to surveys, more than half of those people say that they're going specifically to see the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 我想根据调查，超过一半的人说他们去那里就是为了专门看《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: So it now has its own dedicated room.
sentences.zh: 所以它现在拥有自己专属的房间。

sentences.en: It's got its own kind of crowd management procedures.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的一套人群管理程序。

sentences.en: It's got its own security arrangements.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的安保安排。

sentences.en: But it's still kind of messing up the ability of the Louvre to present all its other paintings,
sentences.zh: 但它仍然在某种程度上干扰了卢浮宫展示其他所有画作的能力，

sentences.en: because the curators in the Louvre have always insisted that the Mona Lisa be presented as a Renaissance painting.
sentences.zh: 因为卢浮宫的策展人一直坚持将《蒙娜丽莎》作为一幅文艺复兴时期的画作来展出。

sentences.en: So alongside other Renaissance paintings.
sentences.zh: 也就是与其他文艺复兴时期的画作摆在一起。

sentences.en: And the effect is that people just, you know, they rush past all the other Renaissance paintings, including Leonardo's picture of John the BaptiSt.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是人们只是匆忙跑过所有其他的文艺复兴画作，包括达芬奇画的《施洗者约翰》。

sentences.en: And they all kind of gather around the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 然后他们全都涌向《蒙娜丽莎》周围。

sentences.en: And so the plan now, this is part of President Macron's kind of Napoleonist ambitions, his grand projet is going to be his kind of final legacy project.
sentences.zh: 所以现在的计划——这是马克龙总统拿破仑式雄心的一部分，他的宏伟项目将成为他个人的最终遗产项目。

sentences.en: And he's called it the new Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 他将其命名为“新文艺复兴”。

sentences.en: So the Mona Lisa is going to be moved to an underground gallery.
sentences.zh: 因此，《蒙娜丽莎》将被移至地下展厅。

sentences.en: It's going to be entirely exclusive to the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 它将完全专属于《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: There will be no other work of art inside it.
sentences.zh: 里面将不会有任何其他艺术品。

sentences.en: And that is scheduled to open in 2031.
sentences.zh: 该项目计划于2031年开放。

sentences.en: So Lisa Gerardini will end up having her very own suite of rooms in the most visited museum in the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，丽莎·盖拉蒂尼最终将在世界上参观人数最多的博物馆里拥有她自己的一套专属展厅。

sentences.en: And I think that I love it that an otherwise entirely obscure Florentine woman is so astronomically insanely famous.
sentences.zh: 我想，我特别喜欢这样一个事实：一个原本完全默默无闻的佛罗伦萨女性竟然拥有如此天文数字般疯狂的名气。

sentences.en: Such an interesting story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此有趣的故事。

sentences.en: And yet I have to say, I find it quite an unbelievably uninteresting painting, but it is a fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 然而我不得不说，我觉得它是一幅难以置信地索然无味的画作，但它确实是一个迷人的故事。

sentences.en: I think the more I trace the history of how it's come to be famous and the many ways in which it's been understood,
sentences.zh: 我想，我越是追溯它如何成名的历史以及人们理解它的诸多方式，

sentences.en: the more you can see that all these, everything that people have seen in it is kind of there.
sentences.zh: 你就越能看出所有这些，人们在其中看到的一切其实都原本就在那里。

sentences.en: I mean, it is kind of infinite in the ways that it can be interpreted and seen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在被解读和看待的方式上可以说是无限的。

sentences.en: And that might not be true of other paintings.
sentences.zh: 其他画作可能就未必如此。

sentences.en: I think the story is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个故事太有趣了。

sentences.en: And it's such an interesting case study in art history and art criticism.
sentences.zh: 它是艺术史和艺术批评中一个如此有趣的案例研究。

sentences.en: But frankly, as a painting, I can think of hundreds of paintings I'd rather look at than the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 但坦率地说，作为一幅画，我想能列出几百幅我更愿意看的画，而不是《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: So anyway, that does not in any way diminish the story, which is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 总之，这丝毫无损于这个故事的精彩迷人。

sentences.en: Tom, merci beaucoup.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，非常感谢。

sentences.en: And arrivederci.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
